# dsh-desktop-notify

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

Desktop notifications for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness).
A Windows toast appears when a Session needs you — and clicking it brings that
Session back to the front.

Two triggers:

| Trigger | When it fires |
| --- | --- |
| **Needs attention** | The Agent is blocked waiting for your approval or your answer. |
| **Run finished** | A Session that was running has stopped, and the run lasted at least `minRunMs`. |

## Install

Requires the **Desktop** application (the Windows toast path depends on Electron
running the renderer; a browser tab has no AppUserModelID to notify under).

### From the DSH plugin page (no terminal)

Open **Settings → Plugins → Add plugin**, and paste one of these into
**Package name or address**:

| What you paste | When to use it |
| --- | --- |
| `github:guanhaisen/dsh-desktop-notify` | Straight from this repository. Nothing published to npm. |
| `https://github.com/guanhaisen/dsh-desktop-notify` | Same thing, written as a URL. |
| `D:\path\to\dsh-desktop-notify` | A local checkout. **Must be an absolute path.** |

Then press **Install**. The plugin manager runs `pnpm add` in your profile, adds
the bundle to the profile's list, and the notification half activates without a
restart in most cases — reload the page (`Ctrl+R`) if the first toast does not
arrive.

> Installing from git resolves the repository's **default branch**. If you fork
> this and your default branch differs, paste the full spec with a ref instead:
> `github:you/dsh-desktop-notify#main`.

> The plugin page states that installed plugins **do not auto-update**: to
> upgrade, uninstall and install again. A `github:` install follows the default
> branch, so reinstalling picks up new commits.

### From the command line

```bash
# In your DSH desktop profile directory:
#   Windows: %USERPROFILE%\.dsh\profiles\desktop
pnpm add github:guanhaisen/dsh-desktop-notify
```

Or link a working copy, so edits apply on save:

```bash
pnpm add link:/path/to/dsh-desktop-notify
```

Either way, the package must then appear in that directory's `package.json`
bundle list — the plugin page does this for you; a manual install does not:

```json
{
  "dsh": {
    "profile": {
      "bundles": ["...existing bundles...", "dsh-desktop-notify"]
    }
  }
}
```

> Keep this package free of runtime `dependencies`. pnpm does not install a
> linked package's own dependencies, and a resolution failure during Cordis tree
> initialisation stops DSH from starting.

### You will not see a toast when…

This is the part that looks like a bug and is not:

| Situation | Why it is silent |
| --- | --- |
| You are looking at that Session | The prompt is already on screen. |
| The run was shorter than `minRunMs` (20 s) | A quick reply is not news. |
| The Session was already running when the window opened | The first snapshot is a baseline, so opening DSH does not fire a burst. |
| Windows **Do Not Disturb** is on | The OS suppresses the banner. The notification still reaches the notification centre. |

If none of those apply and nothing appears, read the decision log — see
[Verifying it actually works](#verifying-it-actually-works). It records every
suppression *with its reason*, so "why did I not get a toast?" is answerable.

## Why this is a plugin and not a shell patch

The obvious implementation — add a `Notification` call to the Electron main
process — cannot work here, and understanding why explains the whole design.

The Desktop Host is **not** the Electron main process. `lib/main.js` spawns it as
a *separate Node child process*:

```js
spawn(this.node, ['--expose-internals', entry, ...], { stdio: ['ignore','pipe','pipe','ipc'] })
```

That child is the Electron executable re-entered in Node mode, so
`require('electron')` inside a Host plugin yields no `Notification`, and the
process holds no AppUserModelID. Meanwhile the shell's own notification code
(`lib/main.js`) only ever fires for one thing: a mandatory update.

The renderer, however, has everything needed:

- `dsh-app:` is registered as a privileged scheme with `standard: true` and
  `secure: true`, making the window a **secure context**, which the Web
  Notification API requires.
- The application session installs a permission handler that returns `true` for
  every non-media permission.

So a plain Web `Notification` in the window becomes a real Windows toast under
the application's own identity (`electron.app.DeepSeek Harness`). No shell
patch, no helper process, and it survives application updates.

## Where the state comes from

Nothing is polled and no second source of truth is created.
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-session` already folds exactly these facts and
publishes them as `ctx.uiSession.sessionStatus`:

```
Map<sessionId, { running, pendingInteraction, completionUnread }>
```

It is fed by the `api-session/status` Remote event. This plugin only reads it.

`pendingInteraction` is the interaction object itself, whose `kind` is one of:

| `kind` | Raised by | Copy shown |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `approval` | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-approval` | Tool named in the request is asking for privileged execution |
| `question` | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-user-questions` | The Agent asked a question |
| `plan-review` | same, when the questions are a plan | A plan is waiting for review |

Its `key` is the identity used to de-duplicate, so a status re-emission for the
same wait never produces a second toast.

## Layout

| File | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `index.js` | Host half. Owns the Loader row the browser half binds to. Registers nothing — no tool, no service, no route. |
| `client.js` | Browser half. Watches Session status, decides when to notify, renders the toast, wires click-through, and publishes the `DesktopNotify` Inspect provider. |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | The one Host row the bundle inserts. |
| `test/watcher.test.mjs` | Behavioural test of the decision logic, runnable with plain `node`. |

## Configuration

Set on the plugin's row in the profile patch, or via the Plugins page:

| Key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `notifyOnAttention` | `true` | Notify when a Session is blocked on you. |
| `notifyOnComplete` | `true` | Notify when a run finishes. |
| `minRunMs` | `20000` | Ignore runs shorter than this. Quick replies are not news. |
| `sound` | `true` | Play the system notification sound. |

### De-duplication

A repeated interaction never re-notifies: identity is the interaction's own
`key`, so a status re-emission for the same pending approval stays silent. The
first snapshot after the window opens is treated as a baseline rather than as
news, which is what stops a launch from firing a burst of toasts for Sessions
that were already running.

## Verifying it actually works

Delivery is asynchronous and visual, and neither half can observe the toast the
operating system renders. So the browser half publishes a Cordis Inspect
provider, `DesktopNotify`, which can be queried from outside the page:

| Method | Answers |
| --- | --- |
| `status` | Is the half mounted? What is `Notification.permission`? Is this a secure context? Which Sessions are tracked, and since when? |
| `testToast` | Fire one real toast now, and report what was constructed. |
| `decisions` | The in-memory decision log — every notification sent *and* every one deliberately suppressed, with the reason. |

`decisions` is the one that answers "why did I not get a toast?": a suppressed
entry carries `suppressed: 'watched'` (you were looking at that Session) or
`suppressed: 'too-short'` (the run ended before `minRunMs`).

The log is **in memory only**, bounded to the last 100 entries. It is
deliberately not written to disk: a file that can silently fail to appear is
worse than no file at all.

### Confirming against the OS

`testToast` reporting `delivered: true` only means a `Notification` was
constructed. To confirm it reached the operating system, compare Windows' own
record for this app's AUMID before and after:

```powershell
$k = 'HKCU:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Notifications\Settings\electron.app.DeepSeek Harness'
[DateTime]::FromFi

plugins.description: Semantic session search backend for DSH, backed by Ollama or any OpenAI-compatible embedding endpoint.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-session-query-vector

A semantic session-search backend for DSH, backed by Ollama or any OpenAI-compatible `/v1/embeddings` endpoint.

DSH ships a SQLite full-text backend (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-query-sqlite`) that answers "which session contained this word". This package replaces it with a vector backend that answers "which session was about this" — you ask in your own words, the query is embedded, and the closest chunks come back with their session and snippet.

It is a drop-in replacement for the official backend: both extend the same `sessionQuery` service, so exactly one of them may be mounted at a time.

## Requirements

| | |
|---|---|
| DSH | `0.2.1-rc.2` (developed and tested against it) |
| `@deepseek-ai/cordis` | `~4.0.5` |
| `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` | `3.18.5` (ships with DSH) |
| Node.js | 22+ — the indexer uses the built-in `node:sqlite` (`DatabaseSync`) |
| An embedding endpoint | Ollama locally, or any OpenAI-compatible API |

Earlier DSH releases are untested.

## Two pieces

| Piece | What it is |
|---|---|
| `lib/index.js` | The **query** side — a `SessionQueryEngine` subclass mounted as a plugin. Answers searches by reading the index. Never embeds. |
| `indexer.mjs` | The **index** side — a standalone script. Walks `~/.dsh/sessions`, embeds the message text, writes the vectors. |

They are deliberately separate: search must stay fast, and embedding is slow. The query side never triggers an embedding on the search path; if the index is empty it returns nothing.

**The two sides must use the same embedding model.** Otherwise the stored vectors and the query vector live in different spaces and every score is noise. Configure `embedModel` identically in both.

## Install

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <your-profile> add github:minhaoli/dsh-session-query-vector
```

The package declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, so `dsh plugin add` appends it to `dsh.profile.bundles` and the loader mounts it on the next start.

**The bundle patch also disables the official backend**, because both register `sessionQuery`:

```yaml
# cordis.patch.yml shipped with this package
- id: session-query-sqlite
  disabled: true

- insert:
    - id: session-query-vector
      name: 'dsh-session-query-vector'
      config:
        provider: ollama
        baseUrl: 'http://127.0.0.1:11434'
        embedModel: bge-m3
        openAt: first-search
```

If you would rather keep the official backend, remove that first row and do not mount this package — they cannot coexist.

## Configuration

Set these in your profile's `cordis.patch.yml`. A patch replaces the targeted row's whole `config` rather than merging into it, so restate every key you want to keep.

```yaml
# ~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml
- insert:
    - id: session-query-vector
      name: 'dsh-session-query-vector'
      config:
        path: 'C:/Users/<you>/.dsh/storages/session-query-vector.sqlite'
        provider: openai
        baseUrl: 'https://api.siliconflow.cn/v1'
        apiKey: 'sk-...'
        embedModel: 'BAAI/bge-m3'
        openAt: first-search
        topK: 20
        minScore: 0.45
```

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | `~/.dsh/storages/session-query-vector.sqlite` | Index database. Created on first use. |
| `openAt` | `first-search` | `startup` opens the DB at mount; `first-search` on the first query; `never` disables search entirely. |
| `provider` | `ollama` | `ollama` or `openai`. `openai` means any OpenAI-compatible `/v1/embeddings`. |
| `baseUrl` | `http://127.0.0.1:11434` | Embedding endpoint. A trailing `/v1` is stripped and re-added, so `https://host/v1` and `https://host` both work. |
| `apiKey` | `""` | Sent as `Authorization: Bearer` when non-empty. Not needed for Ollama. |
| `embedModel` | `bge-m3` | Must match the indexer. |
| `embedTimeoutMs` | `120000` | Per-request timeout. |
| `topK` | `20` | Candidates pulled from the index before ranking. |
| `minScore` | `0.45` | Cosine floor. |
| `relMargin` | `0.10` | Relative cutoff: a hit is kept only if its score is within `relMargin` of the best hit. |
| `snippetChars` | `240` | Snippet length in the result. |
| `readWindowMax` | `50` | Read window for the engine's live-preferred reads. |

## Endpoint contracts

### Ollama (`provider: ollama`)

```http
POST {baseUrl}/api/embeddings
content-type: application/json

{ "model": "bge-m3", "prompt": "the text to embed" }
```

Response: `{ "embedding": [0.013, -0.021, ...] }`.

Pull the model first:

```bash
ollama pull bge-m3
```

### OpenAI-compatible (`provider: openai`)

```http
POST {baseUrl}/v1/embeddings
authorization: Bearer <apiKey>
content-type: application/json

{ "model": "BAAI/bge-m3", "input": ["chunk one", "chunk two"] }
```

Response: `{ "data": [{ "index": 0, "embedding": [...] }, ...] }`. Results are sorted by `data[].index` before use — some providers return them out of order.

A trailing `/v1` on `baseUrl` is stripped before `/v1/embeddings` is appended, so `https://api.siliconflow.cn/v1` does not become `/v1/v1/embeddings`.

Any endpoint that satisfies this contract works: SiliconFlow, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Together, a local vLLM or LM Studio server, and so on. Set `baseUrl`, `apiKey` and `embedModel` to whatever that provider names the model.

## Building the index

`indexer.mjs` is not run by DSH — start it yourself, after the query side is configured. It must be able to `import` the `@deepseek-ai/*` packages, so run it with the DSH runtime (see below).

```bash
# layered: layer 1 (user messages) first, then layer 2 (assistant messages)
node indexer.mjs

node indexer.mjs --layer=1        # only user messages — fastest path to a usable search
node indexer.mjs --layer=2        # only assistant messages
node indexer.mjs --limit=200      # cap sessions this run
node indexer.mjs --status         # print progress, index nothing
node indexer.mjs --force          # re-index unchanged sessions
node indexer.mjs --quiet          # no progress lines, only key events
node indexer.mjs --skip-active=5  # skip sessions written in the last 5 minutes
```

| Environment variable | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `DSH_HOME` | `~/.dsh` | DSH home. Everything else derives from it. |
| `DSH_MODULES` | `$DSH_HOME/node_modules/@deepseek-ai` | Where to resolve `@deepseek-ai/*`. Override for the packaged desktop app. |
| `VEC_DB` | `$DSH_HOME/storages/session-query-vector.sqlite` | Index path — must equal the plugin's `path`. |
| `VEC_SESSIONS` | `$DSH_HOME/sessions` | Session log root. |
| `VEC_PROVIDER` | `ollama` | `ollama` or `openai` — must equal the plugin's `provider`. |
| `VEC_BASE_URL` | `http://127.0.0.1:11434` | Must equal the plugin's `baseUrl`. |
| `VEC_API_KEY` | `""` | Must equal the plugin's `apiKey`. |
| `VEC_MODEL` | `bge-m3` | Must equal the plugin's `embedModel`. |
| `VEC_CHUNK` | `1200` | Characters per chunk. |
| `VEC_BATCH` | `16` | Chunks per embedding request. |
| `VEC_SUBAGENTS` | — | Set to `1` to include subagent sessions. |

### Running the indexer against the packaged desktop app

The Electron app's `@deepseek-ai/*` modules live inside `app.asar`, which plain `node` cannot read. Point `DSH_MODULES` at the asar and run the indexer under the app's own binary in Node mode:

```powershell
$env:ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE = '1'
$env:DSH_MODULES = 'D:/APP/deepseek harness/resources/app.asar/dsh/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/'
& 'D:\APP\deepseek harness\DeepSeek Harness.exe' indexer.mjs --status
```

From a source checkout, plain `node indexer.mjs` works — `DSH_MODULES` already points at real files.

## Index schema

One SQLite file, `application_id = 1146308690` (distinct from the official backend's), `user_version = 1`. A file whose `application_id` belongs to something else is refused rather than clobbered.

| Table | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `vec_chunks(session_id, seq, type, time, chunk_idx, text, dim, vector BLOB)` | One row per embedded chunk. Primary key `(session_id, seq, chunk_idx)`. |
| `vec_sessions(id, revision, indexed_at, chunks, cwd, layer)` | Per-session bookkeeping; `revision` drives the incremental skip. |
| `vec_queries(text, vector, dim, at)` | Query-vector cache, so repeating a search skips the embedding round

plugins.description: 工作区插件门控：插件照常加载，按工作区（目录）把它不该占的提示词前缀摘掉——工具 schema 与提示词段不再进模型上下文。Workspace-scoped plugin gate for DeepSeek Harness (dsh).
plugins.readme_text:
简体中文 ｜ English

# dsh-workspace-gate · 工作区插件门控 > 插件照常加载，但**按工作区**把它不该占的提示词前缀摘掉——工具 schema 与提示词段都不再进模型上下文。 [![version](https://img.shields.io/github/v/tag/M1r0er/dsh-workspace-gate?label=version&color=blue)](https://github.com/M1r0er/dsh-workspace-gate/tags) [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-workspace-gate?label=npm&color=cb3837)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-workspace-gate) [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green)](LICENSE) [![dsh-plugin](https://img.shields.io/badge/topic-dsh--plugin-6f42c1)](https://github.com/topics/dsh-plugin) 一个 [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)（`dsh`）插件。 它让"要不要让模型看见某个插件"从**全局**下沉到**工作区**：插件依然全部加载、功能随时可用， 但在你指定的目录下，它的工具 JSON schema 和系统提示词段不再出现在每一次请求里。 省下的是每轮请求的输入 token，而不是插件的加载开销。 --- ## 目录 - [它解决什么问题](#它解决什么问题) - [它做什么 / 不做什么](#它做什么--不做什么) - [主要特性](#主要特性) - [界面](#界面) - [安装](#安装) - [使用](#使用) - [归属是怎么判断的](#归属是怎么判断的) - [数据存放](#数据存放) - [为什么不是"真·停用插件"](#为什么不是真停用插件) - [实测数据](#实测数据) - [开发](#开发) - [已知边界](#已知边界) - [许可证](#许可证) --- ## 它解决什么问题 DSH 自带的插件管理只有 **全局** 开关：一个插件要么对所有工作区都开，要么都关。 但插件对 prompt 的成本是**每轮都付**的——只要它启用了，它的工具 JSON schema 和 系统提示词段就会出现在每一次请求里，哪怕这次对话完全用不到它。 典型场景： - 装了「小说写作」插件，但你 90% 的时间在写代码； - 装了「网页搜索」全家桶，但某个离线项目根本不该联网； - 学生工作区只需要讲解/脑图，教师工作区只需要备课/教案。 **本插件把"要不要让模型看见"从全局下沉到工作区**，不动全局开关、不重启、不重载插件。 ## 它做什么 / 不做什么 | 做 | 不做 | | --- | --- | | 按目录（含子目录继承）决定哪些工具/段不进 prompt | ❌ 不安装/卸载/升级插件 | | 组级开关 + 展开到单个工具名/段名 | ❌ 不改变插件的全局启用状态 | | 按来源分档：第三方 / 自定义 / 官方 / 官方可选包 | ❌ 不能把全局已停用的插件"变出来"（只减不加） | | 自动归属推断 + 静态扫包 + 手工归属 | ❌ 不回溯已开会话（前缀已经发出去了） | | fail-open：任何异常都当作"没配置" | ❌ 不碰 sandbox / approval 策略 | ## 主要特性 - **工作区级收窄**：配置单位是目录，子目录自动继承最近祖先（给 `D:\Projects` 配一次， `D:\Projects\api` 就继承）。 - **只减不加**：用的是 DSH 最弱的收窄原语 `ctx.tools.restrict()`，它只能移除，不会新增能力。 - **两类可见面都管**：工具 schema + 系统提示词段（后者用"同名空文本段遮蔽"实现）。 - **按来源分档**：靠 bundle 的 `availability` 判断"随 dsh 安装"还是"用户自装"， 第三方档默认展开，官方档默认收起。 - **归属可手工矫正**：每个工具/段右侧有归属下拉，可以把未归属的项并入已有分组或新建分组。 - **模型可调**：`workspace_gate` 工具支持 `status` / `list` / `set`。 - **可控的噪声**：不写 DOM、不加载宿主客户端包、颜色只用 `--dsw-alias-*` 主题 token。 - **可测试**：核心逻辑抽在 `lib/policy.mjs`，24 条单测，不启动 DSH 也能跑。 ## 界面 插件管理页会多出一个 **「按工作区」** 页签： ``` 插件照常加载；勾掉的插件，它的工具与提示词段不再进入这个目录的请求。 存储: ~/.dsh/data/workspace-gate.json [重新扫描] 工作区 (default-workspace) (my-project ●) (+ 添加目录) C:\work\my-project · 跟随全局 · 已关 1 组 · 共 9 组 插件组 [筛选…] › 第三方 2 ≈ 2.7k [网] web-search-free [9 工具][1 段] ≈2.7k › ● › 自定义分组 1 › 官方 7 ≈ 17.8k › 官方可选包 1 › 未归属 27 ``` - 行尾开关 = 这一组在这个目录下是否可见； - `›` 展开后可以只勾单个工具/段，右侧下拉可以改它的归属； - 顶部显示当前目录、是否已单独配置、关了几组、大概省多少 token/轮。 ## 安装 本插件是标准 DSH bundle（`package.json` 里声明 `dsh.bundle.patch`）。 三种装法，**推荐顺序从上往下**；装好后都会在插件管理页出现「工作区插件门控」这一行。 > **已发布到 npm**：[`dsh-workspace-gate@0.1.1`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-workspace-gate)。 > 能访问 npm 的机器可以直接 > `dsh plugin --profile add dsh-workspace-gate@0.1.1`，不必走 GitHub。 > **版本要求**：`engines.dsh = ^0.2.1-rc.2`。比这更老的 DSH 会被插件管理器**直接拒绝安装**， > 而不是装上以后在运行期报错。 ### 方式 1 · 让 AI 帮你装（最省事，推荐新手） 新开一个会话，把这句话发给助手： > 帮我安装这个 DSH 插件：`github:M1r0er/dsh-workspace-gate` 助手会调用 `plugin_manager` 完成「pnpm 安装 → 选中 bundle → 激活」整条链路，最后告诉你 `application: applied`。然后刷新页面即可。 - 前提：当前会话的预设启用了 `plugin_manager` 工具。DSH 默认只在 **Creator** 模式下启用它， 其它预设默认关闭；如果助手说没有这个工具，切到 Creator 再试，或改用方式 2。 - 安装 Host 代码属于高权限操作，会请求一次性授权。 ### 方式 2 · Web 插件页安装（不碰命令行） 1. 打开 DSH 的 **插件** 页； 2. 点安装入口，在 spec 里填 `github:M1r0er/dsh-workspace-gate` （也可以填你本地 clone 的**绝对路径**）； 3. 若弹出 “Allow these scripts and retry”，确认后重试一次； 4. 列表里出现 `dsh-workspace-gate` 即装好，刷新页面； 5. 确认「工作区插件门控」这一行是**开启**状态。 ### 方式 3 · 命令行（知道自己在做什么的人） ```bash # A. 用 dsh CLI（profile 不是 Desktop 时） dsh plugin --profile add github:M1r0er/dsh-workspace-gate # B. 直接进 profile 目录用 pnpm cd ~/.dsh/profiles/ pnpm add github:M1r0er/dsh-workspace-gate # C. 本地目录（开发/调试） git clone https://github.com/M1r0er/dsh-workspace-gate.git pnpm add link:<克隆下来的绝对路径> # D. 从 npm（0.1.1 起可用） dsh plugin --profile add dsh-workspace-gate@0.1.1 ``` > **`--profile ` 决定改哪个 profile 目录**：`--profile web` 改的是 `~/.dsh/profiles/web`， > 而**桌面版 GUI 跑的是 `desktop` profile** —— 装进 `web`，桌面窗口里看不到，两个 profile 的 > 依赖和 `dsh.profile.bundles` 互相独立。要装进桌面版，请用它自己的插件页 > （npm 版 CLI 会拒绝管理 `desktop`）。 > ⚠️ **pnpm 只装依赖，不会把包写进 `dsh.profile.bundles`。** > 少这一步插件不会加载。装完必须再做一件事： > > - 打开 Web 插件页，把 `dsh-workspace-gate` 这个 bundle **打开**；或 > - 手工在 `~/.dsh/profiles//package.json` 的 `dsh.profile.bundles` > 数组末尾加 `"dsh-workspace-gate"`。 > > 然后重启 DSH（没有 HMR 时）才会加载。 装好后：**关掉插件管理页里「工作区插件门控」这一行 = 门控整体不生效**，行为回到未安装状态（fail-open）。 ### 常见坑 | 现象 | 原因 / 处理 | | --- | --- | | 装完插件页没有这一行 | bundle 没被选中：按方式 3 的提示把它加进 `dsh.profile.bundles` | | 返回 `already-installed` | 同 spec 已装过；先在插件页 Remove 再装 | | 桌面版提示 CLI 不接管 | Desktop profile 由 Electron 托管，npm CLI 会拒绝管理它；请用 Web 插件页 | | 安装卡在 build scripts | pnpm 11 默认拦截安装脚本；在弹窗里批准后重试 | | 想在插件市场里搜到 | 仓库已打 `dsh-plugin` topic，但要在市场出现还需被 awesome-dsh-plugin 索引收录（提交 PR） | ## 使用 ### 给人 插件管理 → 「按工作区」→ 选目录 → 关掉不需要的组 → 保存。对**新会话**生效。 ### 给模型 ```text workspace_gate(action:"status") # 最近哪些会话命中了哪个目录、摘掉了什么 workspace_gate(action:"list") # 可门控的插件 → 工具名/段名 workspace_gate(action:"set", dir:"D:\\Projects\\api", hide:["plugin:r18-novel"]) # 需要显式给 dir workspace_gate(action:"set", dir:"D:\\Projects", show:["tool:read"]) # 从隐藏清单移除 ``` > 这个工具没有用 `deferLoading`：实测打开后子会话里它**直接不可见**，模型想调也调不到。 两种写法等价（`dir` 必须是绝对路径，子目录会继承）： - 隐藏整组：`plugin:<分组 id>` - 隐藏单项：`tool:<工具名>` / `section:<段名>` ## 归属是怎么判断的 DSH 运行时**不记录**某个工具是哪个插件注册的（`tools.register()` 只按名字存）， 所以"按插件勾选"只能推断。本插件按强度依次尝试： | 顺序 | 手段 | 说明 | 可靠度 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | 段名命名空间 | `r18-novel:protocol` → `r18-novel`，与插件 id/包名归一后比较 | 高（约定） | | 2 | 工具名前缀 | 工具名 token 与插件 id **或包名** token 的**前导全等**匹配 | 中高 | | 3 | 静态扫包 | 读包入口（第三方递归扫 `.js`）里的 `name: 'x'` 定义位，与未归属工具名求交，**只在唯一命中时采纳** | 较高 | | 4 | 手工归属 | 界面里自己指定，赢过以上全部 | 最高 | 静态扫包解决的是这类情况：`dsh-free-search` 的 profile 行 id 是 `web-search-free`， 而它注册的 `platform_search` / `video_search` / `weather` 等名字里根本不含包名—— 只靠前缀只能认出 1/9，扫包之后 9 个全部归位。 **硬边界**：官方内置包在 `app.asar` 里，磁盘上没有目录，扫不到；运行时动态注册的工具 （没有对应文件插件）也没有包可扫。这些会留在「未归属」，用手工归属分类即可。 ## 数据存放 `/data/workspace-gate.json`（本机示例：`~/.dsh/data/workspace-gate.json`） ```json { "version": 1, "overrides": { "d:/projects/api": ["plugin:r18-novel", "tool:free_search_news"] }, "assignments": { "tool:read": "文件工具" } } ``` - `overrides`：**按工作区**的隐藏清单，键是归一化目录（小写 + `/`），子目录继承最近祖先； - `assignments`：**全局**的手工归属，赢过自动推断，只改分组、不影响"要不要隐藏"； - 文件损坏 / 读不到 → 退化为空配置（全放行），不会让门控把会话搞挂。 ## 为什么不是"真·停用插件" 三条硬理由： 1. **全局状态**。profile 的 `disabled` 是每个 profile 一份，不是每个工作区一份； 两个工作区想一开一关只能来回改文件。 2. **来回改 = 反复重激活**。会触发 Loader 重载，而且同时开两个工作区会互相打架。 3. **那也不省 token**。真停用省的是内存与启动开销；而 token 取决于 prompt 里有什么。 本插件摘的正是"模型侧的东西"，与工作区数量无关。 ## 实测数据 本机 DSH 0.2.0-rc.2 / desktop profile： | 事实 | 数值 | | --- | --- | | 全局可见工具（`tools.schemas(undefined)`） | 19 | | 4 个 preset 作用域并集 | 53 | | 某个具体会话可见工具 | 52–59 | | 提示词段（按 preset 并集取） | 20 | | 插件行总数 | 204 | 两个踩出来的坑： 1. **只查全局会漏掉 34+ 个工具**——多数标准工具由 agent preset 在自己的作用域注册， 清单必须按 preset 逐个 `agentPresets.acquireScope(id)` 取并集。 2. `systemPrompt.assemble()` 是 **async**，不 `await` 只拿到一个空对象。 验证记录（对某个目录隐藏 `tool:read` 与 `section:free-search:engines` 后新开子会话）： ```text bound = { cwd: "D:\\DSH Workspace", key: "d:/dsh workspace", deny: ["weather"], sections: ["free-search:engines"], skipped: [] } weather in agentTools : no free-search:engines in agentSections : no ``` `skipped: []` 说明两个名字都被接受——包括 preset 作用域里的工具，即 `restrict` 对 "继承面"（全局 + 祖先层）有效，不必是全局注册。 ## 开发 ```bash npm run check # node --check 三个入口 npm test # 24 条单测（纯逻辑，不需要 DSH） ``` ``` index.js Host 半：绑定 agent、workspace_gate 工具、HTTP 路由 client.js Client 半：插件页「按工作区」页签 lib/policy.mjs 纯逻辑：目录匹配、归属推断、spec 展开、存储规整 tests/policy.test.mjs 上面那层的单测 cordis.patch.yml 组合包的行声明 locale/{zh,en}.json 插件

# 🛡️ dsh-permission-rules - **1024 store channel**: `npm i -g dsh1024` once, then `dsh1024 plugin --profile web add dsh-permission-rules` (counts toward the [deepseek1024.com](https://deepseek1024.com) install ranking). [![Gitee](https://img.shields.io/badge/Gitee-mirror-c71d23?logo=gitee)](https://gitee.com/perrylink/dsh-permission-rules) [![dshfind](https://dshfind.com/api/badge/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules?metric=downloads)](https://dshfind.com/plugins/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules?ref=badge) [![OpenSSF Scorecard](https://api.securityscorecards.dev/projects/github.com/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules/badge)](https://api.securityscorecards.dev/projects/github.com/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules) **Claude Code-style declarative permission rules for DeepSeek Harness.** *Rules decide what is known. A reviewer model decides what is not.* [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache%202.0-blue.svg)](LICENSE) [![DSH plugin](https://img.shields.io/badge/dsh--plugin-✅-green)](https://github.com/topics/dsh-plugin) [![dsh-doctor](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PerryLink/dsh-plugin-doctor/main/badges/PerryLink__dsh-permission-rules.svg)](https://github.com/PerryLink/dsh-plugin-doctor#verified-徽章) [![DSH Market](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/2BingLing/dsh-market/master/assets/readme/badge-top-rated.svg)](https://dsh.market/) [![Node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%5E22.19%20%7C%7C%20%3E%3D24-brightgreen.svg)](#) [![CI](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules/ci.yml?branch=main&label=CI)](https://github.com/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules/actions) [![Version](https://img.shields.io/github/v/tag/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules?label=version)](https://github.com/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules/releases) [![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-permission-rules)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-permission-rules) [![npm downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/dsh-permission-rules)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-permission-rules) [English](README.md) · [简体中文](README-zh.md) · [Español](README-es.md) · [Português](README-pt.md) · [हिन्दी](README-hi.md) ```sh dsh plugin --profile add dsh-permission-rules ```
--- **📖 Ecosystem knowledge base** — measured data, not marketing: [plugin development guide · plugin-selection data · maintenance criteria](https://perrylink.github.io/dsh-plugin-guide/). ## Install & uninstall - **git channel** (latest `main`): `dsh plugin --profile web add github:PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules` — the `prepare` script builds with production dependencies only. - **npm channel** (published releases): `dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-permission-rules`. - **tarball channel**: `pnpm pack` in this repo, then `dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-permission-rules-.tgz`. - **uninstall**: `dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-permission-rules`. ## ⭐ 如果它帮到了你 这个插件是 [DSH 插件家族](https://github.com/PerryLink)的一员（95 个，全部 Apache-2.0）。如果你在用，**给个 star** —— 它不会解锁任何功能，但会让下一个人在搜索里更容易找到它。 *English:* part of a 95 plugin family for DeepSeek Harness. If it is useful, **a star helps the next person find it** — nothing is gated behind it. ## What is dsh-permission-rules? Claude Code-style declarative permission rules for DeepSeek Harness. Rules decide what is known. A reviewer model decides what is not. ![Terminal demo of dsh-permission-rules: dsh-permission-rules — deny/ask rules in one YAML file](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules/main/docs/assets/dsh-permission-rules-hero.png) ![Animated terminal demo of dsh-permission-rules](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules/main/docs/assets/dsh-permission-rules-demo.gif) *The same run, animated.* ## Compatibility | Surface | Status | |---|---| | Harness | DeepSeek Harness `dsh-v0.2.1-alpha.1` (adapted 2026-09-22, full gate chain): its plugin config is the live settings contract — every field is declared `.volatile()`, the Loader hands `apply` a live reference per field, and a saved edit is committed into the running references WITHOUT remounting the plugin, with out-of-range values refused by the schema before anything is written. A host whose Schemastery predates `volatile()` (before 3.18.3) still mounts and runs this plugin — the fields simply stay ordinary values and the live config form is unavailable — because the marker is applied through a capability probe rather than assumed. `Session.append` on this line still cannot stamp the `ignorable` marker (its third argument is the surface-intent bag, and the envelope field survives for stored-log reads only), so the whole `0.2-alpha` line is pre-checked as unmarked and session-log audit stays disabled by default — `append` reads only `sourceEventSeqs`/`surfaceOp` and freezes the envelope, so it has no code path that could stamp the marker; the earlier `0.1.7-alpha` (adapted 2026-09-22), `0.1.5-rc.2` (adapted 2026-09-09) and `0.1.3-alpha` lines keep the same surface-only append signature, and every `0.2` prerelease is classified with them (a STABLE `0.2.x` release is left to the append probe, so a restored marker surface is adopted without a new plugin release). Those lines' log migrations refuse unclassified plugin events even when marked, so `strip` v1 audit rows before a `0.1.3-alpha` host opens the log and v2 audit rows before a `0.1.5-alpha` host migrates it (native v3 logs only need `repair`). | | Node | `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0` | | Platforms | All (host + web settings client) | | Model | Any (deny/ask reasons surface through tool results) | ## What you get `dsh-permission-rules` puts an ordered **`allow` / `deny` / `ask`** rule list in front of every tool call on the `tools/pre-execute` waterfall — deterministic, instant, auditable, and written by you in plain YAML: - **`deny`** blocks the call; the rule's `reason` becomes the model-visible error. - **`ask`** rides the official approval seam (mount `dsh-auto-review` for a second-model answerer, or a human answers; with neither, the harness fails closed). - **`allow`** (and no-match) strictly delegates via `next()` — downstream listeners are never short-circuited. Every hit **and** every passthrough is audit-logged as a `permissionRules/decision` session event (log-only — nothing extra is injected into the model context). - **Rich matching** — tool-name globs (including `mcp__*`), agent-identity selectors (`main` / `subagent` / `preset:*`), argument key/value globs **or** regexes (with `!pattern` negation and an `absent` key dimension), workspace-relative path globs at **any nesting depth**, `when` host conditions (env vars, platform), and **shell command decomposition** (`argv`: command word, argument tokens, pipeline signature) for token-precise command matching. - **Built-in high-risk baseline** — a shipped deny/ask ruleset (destructive commands, privilege escalation, download-and-execute, sensitive paths) enabled by default and appended after user rules so a nearer user rule can override it; toggle with `builtin.enabled`. - **Hierarchical rule files** — optional `searchUp` merges every `.dsh/rules.yaml` from the session cwd to the filesystem root, nearest first. - **Dry-run rollout** — `enforce: false` audits what the policy *would* do while passing every call through. - **Hot reload** — Chokidar watch with debounce; a broken edit keeps the previous rules, never crashes. On a WSL host, or for a rule file under `/mnt/`, the watch switches to polling because native change events are unreliable there. - **Fail loud** — invalid YAML, unknown actions/fields, bad globs/regexes, backtracking-prone patterns, or more than `maxRules` rules fail the load. ## Rule syntax ```yaml # /.dsh/rules.yaml rules: - match: { tools: [bash, pwsh], params: { command: "git push*" }, paths: ["**/secrets/**"] } action: deny reason: "No pushes from protected paths" - match: { tools: [edit, write] } action: ask reason: "File writes need confirmation" ``` - **Match dimensions** — `tools` (globs, incl. `mcp__*`), `agents` (`main` / `subagent` / `preset:`; unknown identity ne
