plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-ban-wait

One Host plugin that refuses tool arguments which would park the DSH agent loop.

It exists because the shell command timeout is not a ceiling. `pwsh-sandbox`'s
`timeoutMs: 1000` promotes a long command to a background job, but the model can
pass `timeoutMs: 180000` on the call itself and the executor honors it up to
`maxTimeoutMs` (600000 ms by default) — three minutes inside one tool call. The
same class of leak is `job_output { wait: true }`, clamped only by a 10-minute
default. This plugin makes "no single call parks the loop" a property of the
tool registry instead of a property of the model's discipline.

## Files

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `index.js` | the plugin: policy + global `ctx.tools.guard()` |
| `check.mjs` | offline self-check of the policy (30 assertions, no DSH process) |
| `bundle-check.mjs` | pre-install check: replays what the plugin page inspects, with the harness's own patch loader |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | the bundle's patch: inserts the Host-plane row |
| `package.json` | `dsh.bundle.patch` → `cordis.patch.yml`; no dependencies |

## Policy

| Config field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `maxBlockingMs` | `1000` | ceiling for any per-call blocking hint the model supplies |
| `denyWaitTools` | `["job_output"]` | tools whose `wait: true` is refused |
| `timeoutHintTools` | `["pwsh", "bash"]` | tools whose `timeoutMs` / `timeout_ms` is checked against `maxBlockingMs` |
| `requireBackgroundTools` | `[]` | tools that must be called with `run_in_background: true` |

A refusal is a `Error: …` tool result that names the ban, clears the background
job of blame, and states how to re-issue the call, so the model recovers in one
step. An unusable config value is logged and replaced by its default rather than
thrown: a typo here must not fail the instance's boot.

## Install

Through the plugin page — the only channel that keeps the plugin visible in the
inventory with its own toggle:

1. **添加插件** → paste the absolute project directory
   (the checkout you just cloned). A local directory is recognised by
   `isAbsolute()` before any npm-spec parsing and never touches a registry, so
   the registry chooser in that dialog is irrelevant.
2. The manager reads `package.json`, requires a `name` and a `dsh.bundle`, adds
   the dependency to the profile, then reconciles `dsh.profile.bundles`
   automatically ("new bundle dependencies activate automatically"). The plugin
   then appears under 已安装 with a toggle.
3. If the result reports that a restart is required, restart the instance: a new
   Host module generation is not loaded into a running process.

Do **not** also add a raw loader row for this plugin to the profile patch. The
bundle's `cordis.patch.yml` inserts row id `ban-wait`, and two rows sharing that
id make id-targeted patches — the toggle, any override — reach only one of them.

Companion configuration, without which the guard is the only thing standing
between the model and a three-minute call:

```yaml
- id: pwsh-sandbox
  name: "@deepseek-ai/dsh-pwsh-sandbox"
  config:
    timeoutMs: 1000       # default for a command
    maxTimeoutMs: 1000    # ceiling for the model's timeoutMs argument — the line that matters
    maxOutputBytes: 10000
```

## Verify

```powershell
# the policy itself (30 assertions)
node check.mjs

# the package the plugin page will inspect: path, package.json, name, dsh.bundle,
# `files` coverage, and a real parse of cordis.patch.yml by the harness loader
node bundle-check.mjs
```

Neither proves activation — that happens when the profile mounts the bundle's
layer, which the plugin page reports in its install result.

Live probes (each returns a refusal instead of executing):

```
job_output   { job_id: "pwsh-1", wait: true }        → Error: … (ban-wait): job_output was called with wait: true
pwsh         { command: "ok", timeoutMs: 180000 }    → Error: … caps how long one tool call may hold the agent loop at 1000 ms
pwsh         { command: "ok" }                       → runs normally
workflow     { script: "return 1" }                  → runs synchronously (not banned by default)
```

Verified on instance 3080: both refusals fire, plain calls and non-blocking job
reads behave exactly as before, and the row mounts and unmounts live — no
restart was needed for any of it.

## Boundaries

- The guard sees **arguments**, not duration. A tool with no blocking argument
  that simply runs long is out of its reach; that is what `requireBackgroundTools`
  is for, and what the shell `maxTimeoutMs` cap already handles for commands.
- `ask_user_question` is deliberately never banned: blocking on a human is the
  feature.
- `workflow` and a synchronous `subagent` are **not** banned by default. They do
  real work inside the call, so backgrounding them changes how the result is
  consumed. Enable per tool when that trade is wanted:
  ```yaml
  requireBackgroundTools: [workflow, subagent]
  ```

## Superseded

This plugin began as a single-rule ban that refused only `job_output { wait: true }`;
that early version has been folded into the policy shipped here, so there is nothing
left to install separately.

plugins.description: Native Rapid-MLX provider for DeepSeek Harness (dsh) — dsh reads model facts from the server instead of your settings.yaml.
plugins.readme_text:
# @raullenchai/dsh-provider

A native [Rapid-MLX](https://github.com/raullenchai/Rapid-MLX) provider for
[DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) — so `dsh`
gets its model facts from the server instead of from whatever you typed into
`settings.yaml`.

[![CI](https://github.com/raullenchai/rapid-mlx-dsh-provider/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/raullenchai/rapid-mlx-dsh-provider/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

> **Status: published to npm** as
> [`@raullenchai/dsh-provider`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@raullenchai/dsh-provider).
> The end-to-end `dsh` run in [Verified](#verified) was on an M3 Ultra against
> `dsh 0.1.0-rc.7`; `dsh 0.1.0-rc.8` is API-compatible — the `LlmAdapter`
> contract is byte-identical and the only changes are additive — and the
> adapter is re-verified against rc.8 at the protocol and unit-test level.
> DSH is still a developer preview that moves fast, so treat this as tracking
> a moving target, not a frozen compatibility promise.

## What it does for you

DSH can already talk to a local Rapid-MLX server through its generic
`openai-completions` provider. That route works — but it knows nothing about
your model beyond what you hand-wrote:

```yaml
# what the generic route makes you maintain, by hand, per model
llm-pi-ai:
  providers:
    rapid-mlx:
      baseURL: http://localhost:8000/v1
      defaultContextWindow: 262144      # you looked this up. is it still right?
      models:
        - id: qwen3.6-35b-8bit
          contextWindow: 262144
          reasoningEfforts: {off: none, low: low, medium: medium, high: high}
```

Rapid-MLX's `/v1/models` already publishes all of that and more. This adapter
reads it, so:

**1. Nothing to hand-write, and nothing to re-write when you switch models.**
Swap what `rapid-mlx serve` is running and `dsh` follows. No re-running setup,
no stale numbers.

**2. The reasoning control tells the truth.** Rapid-MLX reports whether a model
actually has a reasoning parser. A model that can't reason no longer shows an
off/low/medium/high selector that does nothing.

**3. Compaction is timed with the capacity that actually fits this Mac, not a
number that drifted.** This is the one that quietly costs you.
`dsh-compaction-basic` asks the provider for the route's capacity and compacts
at `thresholdRatio × capacity` (0.8 by default). The provider prefers the
server's **`max_model_len`** — Rapid-MLX's memory-fitted ceiling (what fits in
unified memory: weights + KV cache), in the vLLM/SGLang-standard field — over
the native `context_window`, and falls back to `context_window` on an older
server that doesn't report it. So compaction is timed to what the machine can
actually hold, not the model's advertised window (which it may not have room
for) and not a hand-written number copied from another model.

## Install

Needs Node ≥ 22.15 (dsh imports Node's Zstd stream API without declaring it)
and a running Rapid-MLX server.

```sh
# From npm:
dsh plugin --profile web add @raullenchai/dsh-provider

# …or straight from source — the package ships plain JS with no build step:
dsh plugin --profile web add github:raullenchai/rapid-mlx-dsh-provider

export RAPID_MLX_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8000/v1     # optional; this is the default
dsh web
```

Then point the agent at the route:

```yaml
# $DSH_HOME/settings.yaml
agent-default-model:
  provider: rapid-mlx
  model: qwen3.6-35b-8bit
```

Verified: that command installs and activates as a profile layer against
`dsh 0.1.0-rc.7`. To hack on it locally instead, see
[Local development](#local-development).

## Model management (v0.2.0)

Beyond the provider route, the plugin registers five tools and a `/rapid-mlx`
command so the agent can see and manage models without leaving the session.
The split follows which surface actually owns each fact: served-model facts
come from the structured HTTP `/v1/models`; the download cache and pull/remove
are CLI-only, so those — and only those — shell out to `rapid-mlx` through the
harness subprocess seam.

| Tool | Source | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `rapid_mlx_serving` | HTTP `/v1/models` | The model(s) served right now, deduped, with context window, reasoning/tool parsers, MoE/hybrid, and modalities. |
| `rapid_mlx_cached` | `rapid-mlx models --cached` | Downloaded models and their on-disk size. |
| `rapid_mlx_pull` | `rapid-mlx pull <name>` | Download a model (alias or HF repo id). Cancellable; no fixed deadline. |
| `rapid_mlx_remove` | `rapid-mlx rm -y <name>` | Delete a cached model to free disk. |
| `rapid_mlx_health` | HTTP + `rapid-mlx --version` | API up? CLI reachable? Reported as two independent facts. |

`/rapid-mlx` prints a one-shot overview: health, the served model and its facts,
and total cache disk usage.

The CLI is resolved from the `cliCommand` config (default `rapid-mlx` on
`PATH`, or `$RAPID_MLX_CLI`); set it to an absolute path if the binary is not on
the harness's `PATH`. `rapid_mlx_pull`/`rapid_mlx_remove` are the only tools
that change anything on disk, and they run non-interactively (`rm` is forced
with `-y` because the subprocess seam ignores stdin).

## Verified

Against `dsh 0.1.0-rc.7` on an M3 Ultra:

- Installs and **activates as a profile layer** (no "declares no `dsh.bundle`"
  warning; the entry shows up in `dsh --profile headless --dump-config`).
- Registers the `rapid-mlx` route with `ctx.llm` and serves real queries.
- Plain chat, a single tool call, and the multi-step bug-fix task that gates
  Rapid-MLX releases — the last one fixed the bug and made the target repo's own
  test pass, verified independently, in 36 s on `qwen3.6-35b-8bit`.

## Not done yet

Being explicit, because the point of the adapter is to *use* what the server
says and some of it is still only read:

- `recommended_sampling` — should be applied automatically per model.
- `tool_call_parser` — should let `dsh` fail fast on a model that cannot emit
  `tool_calls`, instead of looping.
- `is_hybrid` / `is_moe` / `capabilities` — read, not yet acted on.
- **Memory-aware capacity.** Today `resolveModel()` reports the model's
  *advertised* context window. On a Mac the real ceiling is unified memory, and
  reporting that instead is the biggest remaining win — it needs Rapid-MLX to
  expose a usable-capacity figure first.
- Images are not carried through `stream()` — but they now **refuse** with
  `LlmError(..., 'UNSUPPORTED')` rather than being dropped, per the cookbook.
  Text, reasoning and tool calls are carried.
- The route is registered as `rapid-mlx`. If your `settings.yaml` also declares
  a `rapid-mlx` provider under `llm-pi-ai`, the two compete for one route name
  (`registerAdapter` owns provider exclusivity). Use one or rename ours.

## Conformance with the official adapter contract

Built against
[`docs/cookbook/adding-an-llm-adapter.md`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/main/docs/cookbook/adding-an-llm-adapter.md)
and its "protocol obligations" section. Each item has a test:

| Obligation | How it is met |
|---|---|
| `usage` before `finish`, nothing after `finish` | usage is buffered and flushed at end-of-stream, so a trailing usage-only chunk cannot reorder it |
| Tool-call `arguments` are raw JSON strings end to end | fragments stream as `argumentsDelta` and reassemble unparsed |
| Block indexes in first-seen order, reused per block | verified across a reasoning-then-text response |
| Errors take exactly two sanctioned paths | transport/protocol failures **throw** `LlmError` with a stable code; nothing ends the stream quietly |
| Honor `options.signal` | passed to `fetch` and to the SSE reader; an `AbortError` is re-thrown unchanged, not reclassified |
| A field the provider cannot honor throws `UNSUPPORTED` | image content refuses instead of being narrowed away |
| Config is a schemastery schema with env fallback | `export const Config`, fed from `cordis.patch.yml` via `!!js process.env.RAPID_MLX_BASE_URL` |

`finish.replayState` is not emitted: Rapid-MLX needs no native response ids
or signatures on follow-up calls, so there is nothing lossless to project.

plugins.description: DeepSeek Harness plugin: semantic search over a personal music and video library, with timecodes, plus a guard that refuses to move, rename or delete media.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-midia

Semantic search over a personal music and video library, with timecodes, inside
[DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness).

Describe what you want to hear or see, in plain language:

> "slow jazz for studying" · "a heavy metal riff, aggressive" · "the moment someone speaks with Portuguese subtitles indoors"

and get the closest tracks and video slices, each with a score and, when the
media was sliced, the timecode. The search is local and read-only: the plugin
never uploads media, and a guard refuses any tool that tries to move, rename or
delete files under the library roots.

| Surface | Name | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| tool | `midia_buscar` | natural-language description → items with score and timecode |
| command | `/midia` | the same search, plus direction arithmetic: `--mais calm --menos drums` |
| command | `/midia-parecidas` | "more like this": nearest items to one example |
| command | `/midia-duplicatas` | three duplicate layers (md5 → SimHash → embedding); proposes, never deletes |
| hook | guard | refuses to move, rename or delete media under the configured library roots |
| skill | `midia` | when to use the search and what it cannot see |

## Install

The plugin is plain Node and runs wherever the harness runs. The install commands
below work in any shell; the slicer (`scripts/fatiar.sh`) needs bash, ffmpeg and
ffprobe.

```sh
# 1. pnpm (the harness manages profile plugins with it)
npm install -g pnpm

# 2. add the plugin to your `web` profile
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web add github:songjongdevsecops/dsh-midia

# 3. restart the harness: the bundle layer is read at boot
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web
```

If `dsh` is already installed globally, step 2 is
`dsh plugin --profile web add github:songjongdevsecops/dsh-midia`.

After the restart the tool, the commands and the guard are live. The package
declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, so `dsh plugin add` appends `dsh-midia` to
`dsh.profile.bundles` in the profile manifest; that line is the activation and is
applied at every boot.

There is no build step and no native dependency: plain ESM using Node built-ins
(`node:fs`, `node:path`, `node:os`, `node:child_process`).

### Update and uninstall

```sh
# update: re-run the add command, then restart
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-midia   # uninstall, then restart
```

## Requirements

The plugin is a reader. It does not embed anything at query time: it asks a local
**EmbeddingGemma** CLI to search an index that already exists on disk. The engine
is not part of this package.

- Node.js `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0` (the range DeepSeek Harness supports).
- pnpm on `PATH`, and DeepSeek Harness itself.
- **EmbeddingGemma CLI** with its models installed on this machine. Default
  binary: `~/workspaces/tools/embeddinggemma/bin/embeddinggemma`; point
  elsewhere with `DSH_MIDIA_GEMMA` or the `gemma` config key.
- **An index** for the collection you search. Build it once with the engine:

  ```sh
  embeddinggemma indexar ~/Media/music --nome mymusic-gemma-v1
  ```

  The engine writes `indices/<name>.npz` next to its own `bin/`, and the plugin
  looks there. The collection name must end in `-gemma-v1` (audio, image, video)
  or `-bgem3-v1` (text, via memsearch).
- Optional: **memsearch** (`~/.local/bin/memsearch`) only for `-bgem3-v1`
  collections.
- Optional: **ffmpeg/ffprobe**, only to slice media before indexing. Timecodes
  exist only for sliced media; see [Timecodes](#timecodes).

## Configuration

Precedence is **profile config → environment variable → default**. `~` is
expanded to your home directory. Defaults follow the reference layout under your
home directory; set yours to match where your media and engine actually live.

| Key | Environment variable | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `musicas` | `DSH_MIDIA_MUSICAS` | `~/workspaces/midia/musicas` | music library root (guard and returned paths) |
| `videos` | `DSH_MIDIA_VIDEOS` | `~/workspaces/midia/videos` | video library root |
| `gemma` | `DSH_MIDIA_GEMMA` | `~/workspaces/tools/embeddinggemma/bin/embeddinggemma` | EmbeddingGemma binary |
| `estado` | `DSH_MIDIA_ESTADO` | `~/workspaces/harness/global/scripts/embeddings/.estado` | optional index state sidecars (granularity note) |
| `memsearch` | `DSH_MIDIA_MEMSEARCH` | `~/.local/bin/memsearch` | memsearch CLI, for `-bgem3-v1` |
| `colecao` | — | `midia-gemma-v1` | collection searched by default |
| `n` | — | `10` | items returned when the model does not pass `n` |
| `guarda` | — | `true` | library guard on/off |

Override by `id` in your profile patch (`~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`).
A patch replaces the whole config of the line, so restate every key you want to
keep:

```yaml
- id: midia
  config:
    colecao: mymusic-gemma-v1
    n: 10
    guarda: true
    musicas: ~/Media/music
    videos: ~/Media/video
    gemma: ~/tools/embeddinggemma/bin/embeddinggemma
```

Environment variables are handy when the engine lives outside the default place:

```sh
export DSH_MIDIA_GEMMA="$HOME/tools/embeddinggemma/bin/embeddinggemma"
export DSH_MIDIA_MUSICAS="$HOME/Media/music"
```

## Usage

In the chat:

```text
/midia slow jazz for studying -n 5
/midia --mais calm --menos drums
/midia-parecidas "/home/you/Media/music/kind-of-blue.flac"
/midia-duplicatas --camada todas --propor
```

Or let the agent call `midia_buscar` with a description. Each returned item has a
name, an absolute path when it can be resolved, a score, a type (`faixa`,
`trecho`, `quadro`) and, for slices, the timecode (`HH:MM:SS` plus the start in
seconds).

The direction arithmetic (`--mais` / `--menos`) is not normalized by the engine:
only the **order** is meaningful there, not the absolute scores.

`/midia-duplicatas` runs three layers: identical bytes (md5), same recording in
another format (SimHash over `strings`), and near-duplicate vectors (cosine). It
writes a proposal under
`${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/dsh-midia/<date>-duplicatas/` and never
touches the media. The optional model verdict (`--llm`) is not implemented; the
three mechanical layers are.

### The guard

While `guarda` is true, the plugin listens on `tools/pre-execute` and denies a
`bash` command whose verb is destructive (`rm`, `mv`, `rename`, `unlink`,
`shred`, `truncate`, `dd`) when it targets a media file under `musicas` or
`videos`. Read-only commands (`ffprobe`, `ls`, `find`, indexers) pass. The guard
covers the `bash` tool only — other tools are not inspected — and paths outside
the configured roots are not its business.

## Timecodes

The EmbeddingGemma **truncates audio at about 30 seconds**: a whole track is
indexed as its first ~30 s, which answers "which song is this", not "at what
moment". Timecodes exist only where the media was sliced, with the second in the
file name:

- audio windows: `<relative path>__t<seconds>.<ext>`, 30 s each;
- video frames: `<relative path>__q<seconds>.jpg`, one frame every N seconds.

The package ships the slicer (`scripts/fatiar.sh`, needs ffmpeg/ffprobe). Clone
the repo to use it, then index the slices folder with the engine:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/songjongdevsecops/dsh-midia.git
cd dsh-midia

# slice from the library root, so the labels stay relative to it
scripts/fatiar.sh --origem ~/Media/video --destino ~/Media/video-slices \
  --janela 30 --quadro-cada 10 --audio-video

embeddinggemma indexar ~/Media/video-slices --nome myvideo-gemma-v1
```

Never index a whole video file as a single item: it becomes one blurred vector.

## Verification

After the restart, run a search in the chat:

```text
/midia calm instrumental jazz
```

- **Items with score, path and, for slices, timecode** — the plugin, the engine
  and the index agree.
- **`motor de mídia ausente: <path>`** — the engine is not where the plugin
  looked. Fix `gemma` / `DSH_MIDIA_GEMMA`.
- **`índice ausente: <path>`** — the collection is not built. Run
  `embeddinggemma indexar ... --nome <collection>` as described in
  [Requirements](#requirements).
- **Paths but no timecode** — the collection was built from whole files; slice
  and re-index as described in [Timecodes](#timecodes).

## Limits

| Limit | Cons

plugins.readme_text:
# DeepSeek Harness Threads

DeepSeek Harness（DSH）侧边线程对话插件，提供独立回复面板及可选的 Slack 风格聊天界面。点击任意一轮回答下的「回复」，即可在右侧栏继续追问。

当前版本：**0.13.9** · 包名：`dsh-threads` · [版本下载](https://github.com/LeoAndJellyfish/DeepSeek-Harness-Threads/releases/tag/v0.13.9) · [问题反馈](https://github.com/LeoAndJellyfish/DeepSeek-Harness-Threads/issues)

## 安装

### Web 版（`dsh web`）

从 GitHub 安装固定版本：

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile web add github:LeoAndJellyfish/DeepSeek-Harness-Threads#v0.13.9
```

安装完成后重启 `dsh web`，刷新浏览器。在一轮已完成的回答下确认「回复」入口，在对话标题栏确认「线程」按钮及 Slack 样式开关。

安装开发分支当前版本：

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile web add github:LeoAndJellyfish/DeepSeek-Harness-Threads
```

### 官方桌面客户端

在 DSH 桌面端会话中发送以下指令，由宿主内置的 `plugin_manager` 安装到当前桌面 profile：

```text
请使用当前桌面端内置的 plugin_manager 安装
github:LeoAndJellyfish/DeepSeek-Harness-Threads#v0.13.9。
先检查当前 profile 和已安装的同名插件，已有安装时核对来源与版本；
通过工具支持的安装或更新操作完成，并报告实际安装版本和重启要求。
```

桌面端使用宿主管理的 `desktop` profile；上述 `--profile web` 命令用于独立 Web 版。安装后按宿主提示重启，随后检查回复入口。

### 离线资源包

下载 Release 中的 `dsh-threads-0.13.9.tgz`，在文件所在目录执行：

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-threads-0.13.9.tgz
```

也可下载 ZIP，解压后使用包含 `package.json` 的目录绝对路径：

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile web add "file:D:/Plugins/dsh-threads"
```

Release 附带 `SHA256SUMS`，可通过 `Get-FileHash <文件路径> -Algorithm SHA256` 核对下载文件。

### 更新与卸载

更新时使用原安装来源及目标版本，优先通过宿主插件管理界面的更新入口操作。早期本地开发包名为 `@local/dsh-threads`，迁移到公开包前应通过对应 profile 的插件管理入口移除旧注册，再安装 `dsh-threads`。线程和文字草稿存放于 `$DSH_HOME/dsh-threads/store.json`，迁移前可备份该文件。

Web 版卸载：

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-threads
```

### 运行条件

插件使用 DSH 的会话分叉、右侧栏、聊天节点插槽和 Markdown 模块。客户端声明为 `web`，由 DSH Web 界面加载；官方桌面端通过内置 Web 界面加载。宿主版本升级可能调整这些接口。

## 功能

- 独立线程面板：会话分叉、归档恢复、工具审批、Markdown 与数学公式。
- 线程导航：回复条数、运行状态、未读提示、最近更新时间。
- 消息输入：文字草稿持久化、粘贴与拖拽图片、线程结论引用。
- 可选 Slack 样式：DeepSeek 账号头像与鲸鱼助手标、日期分隔、悬停操作条、折叠插话，以及 `/goal` 命令输入与结果卡片。
- Host 持久化：线程索引、文字草稿和界面偏好在重启后保留。

## 用法

1. 刷新页面（安装/升级后需要一次）。
2. 把鼠标移到任意一条**已完成**回答的底部动作行，点气泡图标「回复」。
3. 右侧栏出现「线程」页签：顶部引用被回复的那条回答，下面是回复流和输入框。
4. 第一次发送时才真正创建线程——它是一条从该轮分叉出来的子会话，继承到该轮为止的上下文。
5. 线程存在后，该轮下方会常驻一行「N 条回复」，点它随时回到线程。

## 它是怎么实现的

| Slack | DSH |
|---|---|
| Channel | 会话（Session） |
| 一条消息 | 一轮对话（用户提问 + 助手回答） |
| Thread | 从该轮 fork 出的子会话（`parentSession` 指向主会话） |
| Thread 面板 | 右侧栏 `thread` 页签 |

- 线程索引（主会话 + 锚点 seq → 子会话）及文字草稿持久化于 Host 侧 `$DSH_HOME/dsh-threads/store.json`，浏览器 `localStorage` 提供运行内兜底。对话内容存在子会话日志中；草稿发送成功后清空。
- 助手回复用宿主自己的 Markdown 渲染器（`@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-primitives` 的 `MarkdownText`，web shell 静态模块表提供），和聊天区同一套：CommonMark、KaTeX 数学公式、代码块高亮/复制、脚注。引用卡片也用同一渲染器。
- 每条发进线程的消息都会带一段 `<dsh-thread>` 前缀，告诉分叉出来的 agent「你在侧边线程里，回复只有线程面板能看到」。面板渲染时会把这段前缀剥掉；如果直接用「打开子会话」进主界面，会看到原始前缀。
- 子会话会以缩进形式出现在左侧栏，标题沿用分叉时的递增标题。
- 线程会话在左侧栏被归档后，面板会禁用输入框、显示「已在左侧栏归档」提示，并给一个「恢复会话」按钮；草稿保留，恢复后可直接继续。
- 线程里的 Agent 请求工具确认时，面板底部直接出现审批卡片（工具名、理由、「允许一次 / 拒绝」），和主界面审批 UI 读的是同一份 `PendingApproval` 状态。
- 对话标题栏的「线程」按钮打开本会话的线程列表（按最近更新排序，点一行跳到对应线程页签）。
- 线程页签标题是动态的：显示被回复回答的前 18 个字，同时开几条时能分清。
- 线程面板的「带回主对话」把线程最后一条回答以引用块写进主对话输入框（不直接发送，你自己决定发不发、改不改）。
- 线程输入框支持粘贴/拖拽图片，按宿主默认限制：最多 20 张、单张 20 MB；超过 2048px 长边或 4 MP 的图会先在浏览器里缩放（WebP，透明底转白）再发送。
- 线程子会话继承父会话的 Agent 预设（Host 半边在子会话创建、Agent 尚未产生时写入 `agent-preset/selected`；注册表重建 Agent 读的正是这个投影，因此不受 `agentPresets.select()` 的「已开始」限制）。
- 左侧栏里属于线程的子会话行前会显示线程小图标，和普通分支会话区分开。
- 对话标题栏的 Slack 开关（胶囊 + 滑动方块，`role="switch"`）切换消息行样式：Slack 模式下 `user`、`assistant-step`、`steering` 换成头像 + 作者 + 时间的 Slack 行，其余节点仍由宿主渲染；随时可切回原生。
- Slack 行悬停出现整行高亮和浮动操作条（复制、回复进线程、从这个回答分支）。
- Slack 模式下按天插入日期分隔（「今天」「昨天」或「10 月 8 日 星期四」，跨年带年份）；首条消息也显示。
- 用户消息恢复文件卡片（名称/类型/大小）、引用摘要（`referenceLabels`）与技能名（`skillNames`）。
- 中途插入的消息（`steering`）渲染成单行「插话」折叠行，点击展开，不再撑成一条完整消息。
- 线程卡片显示运行中圆点（脉冲）、未读圆点，并在线程完成时刷新条数与最后回复时间。
- 线程输入框可勾选「同时发到主对话」，把这条线程消息以 `[来自线程]` 前缀也发进父会话（会触发父 Agent 回复）。
- 线程面板头部显示最后回复时间与参与者头像，失败时提供「重试」。
- 图片点击打开灯箱（点背景或 Esc 关闭）；正文链接、引用块、代码块使用爵士配色。
- 工具与过程行保留宿主富卡片，只通过 `data-chat-flow-kind` 把外壳缩进对齐到 Slack 正文（Slack 模式下生效）。

## 已知边界

- 线程继承锚点之前的完整上下文，每次回复的输入 token 会变大（前缀缓存可抵消一部分）。
- 「带回主对话」只写草稿，不会自动发送；主对话输入框原有的文字会被保留并接在后面。
- 面板只渲染用户/助手文本（助手部分走完整 Markdown），工具调用折叠成一行，不渲染完整工具卡与轨迹。
- 审批卡片只支持宿主的临时决定（允许一次 / 拒绝）；持久权限策略仍由宿主侧处理。
- 图片只支持图片类型、只存在内存里（切换/重载后需重新粘贴；文字草稿仍然持久化），不支持文件上传。
- 线程列表和索引、草稿、皮肤偏好统一存在 Host 侧 `$DSH_HOME/dsh-threads/store.json`（经 `/dsh-threads/store` 读写，和页面同一套来源/身份校验），端口变化和重启都不丢；`localStorage` 只是同一次运行内的兜底。
- 皮肤偏好与线程索引一起持久化在 Host store；目前替换了 `user` / `assistant-step` / `steering` 三类节点，工具卡、过程行仍由宿主渲染；被替换的行暂未提供宿主原有的编辑/重发交互（复制、回复、分支已补）。
- 有插话的轮次过程组会被宿主强制展开（`hasInterleavedInput`），无法从节点渲染器改变；要改需接管 `conversation.chat.flow`，暂缓。
- 深色模式的对比度只做了静态检查的一部分：亮色下 `#14ADFF` 对白底仅 2.48，已改用深一档的 `--sk-azure-ink` 承担文字；深色块的 token 解析仍未验证。
- Markdown 渲染器来自宿主的静态模块表（`dsh.client.external` 声明）；宿主大版本改名时这里需要跟着改，缺省会退化为纯文本。

## 文件

- `client.js` — 全部客户端逻辑：线程索引、回复入口、右侧面板、Slack 皮肤。
- `index.js` — Host 半边：`/dsh-threads/store` 持久化路由 + 线程子会话的 Agent 预设继承。
- `cordis.patch.yml` — 安装入口。

plugins.description: Liquid-glass skin for DeepSeek Harness: layered glass surfaces, time-of-day wallpapers, theme color and per-layer controls. · DSH 液态玻璃皮肤插件
plugins.readme_text:
# Liquid Glass for DeepSeek Harness

A layered liquid-glass skin for the DSH web UI. Sidebar, conversation column, right rail, pages,
composer, conversation header and settings menus are re-materialised as glass; the page background
becomes a wallpaper that rotates with the time of day; a small sun button in the bottom-right corner
opens the control panel.

Every glass surface is generated by one contract (displacement map → blur → contrast → brightness →
saturation → rim), so any layer at any setting is the same material as the sample capsule.

## What you get

- **13 adjustable glass regions** — sidebar, conversation column, right rail, in-column pages, home
  hero, composer, question card, conversation header, selection highlight, new-session rows, composer
  controls, dialogs & menus, and the draggable sample capsule.
- **14 knobs per region** — tint, tint saturation, concentration, blur, contrast, brightness,
  saturation, rim strength, displacement scale, chromatic aberration and friends. Every knob actually
  moves something; there are no dead sliders.
- **Time-of-day wallpapers** — three bundled images rotate by clock (04:00–11:59 / 12:00–17:59 /
  18:00–03:59), re-checked every 30 s. Four more bundled images ship as ordinary wallpapers: pick one
  to pin it, delete it, or upload your own. Uploads and deletes are written to disk.
- **Four theme colours** — official DeepSeek blue (default), gold, white, black. Applied to the host
  colour ramp and to the new-session layer.
- **Selection highlight** — the active sidebar row or settings nav cell carries glass; switching sends
  a lens flying from the old position to the new one (spring, stretch, trail).
- **Scheme-aware concentration** — tint concentration and brightness follow the light/dark scheme on
  the seven large surfaces, so a light scheme does not get a heavy wash.
- **Bundled font** — HarmonyOS Sans SC (three weights) is served from the package and published as
  `--dsw-font-family`; nothing is installed system-wide and uninstalling removes it.

## Install

```sh
dsh plugin add @istarry/dsh-ui-liquid-glass
```

Then restart the DSH service (fully quit the desktop app, or restart `dsh web`).

## Use

Click the sun button in the bottom-right corner:

- **主题 / Theme** — wallpapers, theme colour, text colour.
- **控件 / Controls** — one tab per region, 14 knobs each, plus a shared sample capsule.

Every value persists automatically. There is a reset per page and a full reset.

## Permissions and behaviour

Read this before installing — the plugin is not a passive stylesheet:

- **Writes to disk.** It creates `~/.dsh/ui-liquid-glass/wallpapers` on first activation and seeds it
  with the bundled wallpapers, adding only files that are missing (never overwriting yours). The
  `Default/` subfolder is kept in sync with the bundled rotation set and is pruned; the root of that
  folder is yours and is never pruned.
- **Serves HTTP routes** on the host web server: `GET /ui-liquid-glass/wallpapers` (list),
  `GET /ui-liquid-glass/wallpapers/<name>` (bytes), `POST` / `DELETE` on the same path (add / remove),
  and `GET /ui-liquid-glass/fonts/<file>` for the bundled font. Hosts without a web server never
  resolve these routes; the picker then hides upload/delete.
- **Overrides host CSS tokens.** It publishes `--lg-*` variables, remaps a number of official
  `--dsw-*` tokens (backgrounds, menu surfaces, hover fills) and sets `--dsw-font-family`. Everything
  is scoped under `body[data-lg-skin]`, so removing the plugin restores the official look.
- **Stores preferences in localStorage** under `ui-liquid-glass/skin/v4` (browser side only).

## Compatibility

- Tested against DSH `0.2.0-rc.2`.
- Peer dependency: `@deepseek-ai/cordis` `^4.0.1`.
- The client half is a self-contained bundle and declares no `dsh.client.inject`; it hooks only
  official CSS tokens, official layout local names, and ARIA roles.

## Bundled assets and licences

- **HarmonyOS Sans SC** — Copyright 2021 Huawei Device Co., Ltd. Redistributed unmodified under the
  HarmonyOS Sans Fonts License Agreement, which permits bundling with software. The full licence is at
  `assets/fonts/LICENSE_Fonts.txt`. The font files must not be modified or redistributed standalone.
- **Wallpapers** — bundled for demonstration. If you repackage or redistribute this plugin, replace
  them with images you have the rights to.

## Building from source

The repository ships prebuilt `lib/` output, so installing from the repository never runs a build.
To rebuild locally you need a DSH source checkout — `tsconfig.json` extends the host's
`tsconfig.base.client.json` and `tsdown.config.ts` imports the host's client preset:

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm exec tsc -b .
pnpm exec tsdown
```

The package name in `tsdown.config.ts` is written into the emitted bundle
(`window.__ModuleLoader__.load({ id })`) — renaming the package means editing that file and rebuilding.

## License

MIT. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).

plugins.description: DeepSeek Harness (DSH) 0.2.1+ compatibility build of @memtensor/memos-local-plugin — installable via dsh plugin add
plugins.readme_text:
# @memtensor/memos-local-plugin

> Reflect2Evolve memory plugin for AI agents.
> One algorithm core, with adapters for OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, and DeepSeek
> Harness.

## What it is

A local-first, file-backed memory system that gives an agent four cooperating
layers of memory and a feedback-driven self-evolution loop:

- **L1 trace** — step-level grounded records (action + observation + reflection + value).
- **L2 policy** — sub-task strategies induced across many traces.
- **L3 world model** — compressed environmental cognition derived from L2 + L1.
- **Skill** — callable, crystallized capabilities the agent can invoke directly.

The plugin learns continuously from two feedback channels:

- **Step-level** — model ↔ environment (tool result, observation deltas).
- **Task-level** — human ↔ model (explicit ratings + implicit signals).

Reflection-weighted reward is back-propagated along each trace, and high-value
patterns crystallize into reusable Skills. At inference time, a three-tier
retriever (Skill → trace/episode → world model) injects the right context at
the right time.

## Layout (high-level)

```
apps/memos-local-plugin/
├── agent-contract/      # Stable types + JSON-RPC protocol shared with adapters
├── core/                # Agent-agnostic algorithm (memory, reward, retrieval, skill, hub, …)
├── server/              # HTTP + SSE server (powers the viewer)
├── bridge.cts + bridge/ # JSON-RPC bridge (used by Hermes Python adapter)
├── adapters/openclaw/   # In-process TS adapter for OpenClaw
├── adapters/hermes/     # Python adapter that talks to bridge.cts
├── adapters/deepseek-harness/ # In-process Cordis bundle for DSH
├── templates/           # config.yaml templates copied to the user's home on install
├── viewer/              # Runtime viewer (Vite, served by server/)
├── docs/                # Developer-facing docs (algorithm, data model, prompts, …)
├── scripts/             # Build / packaging / release helpers
└── tests/               # unit / integration / e2e (vitest)
```

For the full structural breakdown read [ARCHITECTURE.md](./ARCHITECTURE.md).

## Where data lives

Runtime code and user state stay separate. `install.sh` creates the OpenClaw
and Hermes homes; DSH installs the package into a profile with `dsh plugin`
and initializes its runtime home on first boot:


| Agent | Code installed to | Runtime data + config in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OpenClaw | `~/.openclaw/plugins/memos-local-plugin/` | `~/.openclaw/memos-plugin/` |
| Hermes | `~/.hermes/plugins/memos-local-plugin/` | `~/.hermes/memos-plugin/` |
| DeepSeek Harness | Profile dependency managed by `dsh plugin` | `$DSH_HOME/memos-plugin/` (default `~/.dsh/memos-plugin/`) |


Inside the runtime folder:

```
config.yaml      # MemOS core config (includes API keys; chmod 600 when written)
data/memos.db    # SQLite (L1/L2/L3/Skill/Episode/Feedback/…)
skills/          # crystallized skill packages
logs/            # rotating logs (memos.log, error.log, audit.log, llm.jsonl, perf.jsonl, events.jsonl)
daemon/          # bridge pid/port files
```

An adapter creates only the directories it uses. DSH runs `MemoryCore` and the
existing HTTP/SSE Viewer in the DSH Node.js process, without a JSON-RPC bridge
or sidecar daemon. The Viewer listens on `http://127.0.0.1:18801` by default;
set `viewerEnabled: false` in the DSH Cordis row to run without that listener.
DSH still leaves MemOS file logging to the host, so its normal runtime surface
is an optional `config.yaml`, `data/`, and `skills/` when skills are produced.

Uninstalling the plugin does not delete `data/`, `skills/`, `logs/`, or
`config.yaml`. Startup after an upgrade may migrate the SQLite schema, so back
up the runtime directory before upgrading.

## Quick start

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Do not run `npm install -g @memtensor/memos-local-plugin`.**
> This is an agent plugin package, not a standalone CLI. A global
> npm install only downloads the published tarball into your `node_modules`
> tree; it does not wire OpenClaw, Hermes, or DSH. The tarball ships the built
> runtime plus the source and metadata required by the agent installers; the
> `viewer/` source, `website/`, tests, and other development-only files remain
> in this repository.
> Use `install.sh` / `install.ps1` for OpenClaw or Hermes. For DeepSeek
> Harness, use the Unix installer's `--agent dsh` target or DSH's
> lower-level `dsh plugin` command.

For OpenClaw and Hermes, the installer downloads the package from npm, deploys
it to the right agent directory, installs production dependencies, writes the
initial `config.yaml`, and restarts the agent runtime when needed.

From this repository:

```bash
cd apps/memos-local-plugin
bash install.sh --version 2.0.0
```

Or run against the latest published package:

```bash
bash install.sh
```

The installer auto-detects OpenClaw and Hermes. In an interactive terminal it
asks which agent to install for; in non-interactive environments it installs for
the detected agent(s). To test a local package before publishing, pass the
tarball path instead of a registry version:

```bash
npm pack
bash install.sh --version ./memtensor-memos-local-plugin-1.0.0-beta.1.tgz
```

For OpenClaw, use the installer for local archives too:

```bash
bash install.sh --agent openclaw --version ./memtensor-memos-local-plugin-2.0.16-beta.1.tgz
```

Do not substitute `openclaw plugins install ./package.tgz` for this command:
that raw-archive path can resolve development-only DeepSeek peer dependencies
and fail with `ERESOLVE`, including on OpenClaw 2026.9.1 and 2026.9.2.
The installer stages production dependencies and rebuilds `better-sqlite3`.
OpenClaw's newer `npm-pack:` path avoids the peer-resolution conflict, but a
successful managed install alone does not verify native bindings or initialize
MemOS runtime configuration; the installer above remains the supported setup.

When upgrading OpenClaw itself, migrate retired host configuration with
`openclaw doctor --fix` before installing MemOS. The MemOS installer removes its
own legacy `plugins.installs` records, preserves other plugins' old-host records,
and uses the host CLI for capability consent when available. It does not rewrite
the host's internal installation database. See
[the compatibility test results](docs/OPENCLAW-COMPATIBILITY.md) for tested versions
and limits.

On Windows, run `install.ps1` from PowerShell instead of `install.sh` for
OpenClaw or Hermes. The DSH one-command target currently supports macOS/Linux;
Windows users can use DSH's lower-level `dsh plugin` flow.

### DeepSeek Harness

DSH support is an out-of-tree Cordis bundle. The one-command installer keeps
DSH in control of its profile while handling pnpm's reviewed native dependency
build policy non-interactively. If `pnpm` is not already on `PATH`, it prepares
an isolated `pnpm@11.7.0` for that installer run without changing the user's
global package-manager setup:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MemTensor/MemOS/main/apps/memos-local-plugin/install.sh \
  | bash -s -- --agent dsh --profile web --version 2.0.16
```

The installer delegates package ownership and bundle reconciliation to
`dsh plugin`. If pnpm reports the reviewed build-script set, it enables
`better-sqlite3`, `esbuild`, `onnxruntime-node`, and `sharp`, explicitly
disables the unnecessary `protobufjs` and MemOS hint scripts, retries the same
package spec, and verifies the composed `memos-local-memory` row. Any unknown
build-script package fails closed for manual review; the installer never uses
`approve-builds --all`.

The temporary pnpm is removed when the installer exits. It is not needed for
normal `dsh --profile ...` runtime use. Users who later run lower-level
`dsh plugin` commands directly still need pnpm on `PATH`; install the DSH-pinned
version persistently with `npm install -g pnpm@11.7.0` if desired.

To develop from a local checkout instead, build it and add it to the desired
DSH profile directly:

```bash
cd /path/to/MemOS/apps/memos-local-plugin
npm install
npm run build:package
dsh plugin --profile web add .
```

The adapter reuses the provider/model and credentials already configured in
DSH for MemOS auxiliary L

plugins.description: Windows DSH bundle: route the pwsh tool to PowerShell 7, with per-user detection/install and sandbox-aware execution.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-plugin-pwsh7

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-plugin-pwsh7.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-plugin-pwsh7)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/dsh-plugin-pwsh7.svg)](https://github.com/drliuhuan/dsh-plugin-pwsh7/blob/main/LICENSE)

Windows DeepSeek Harness (DSH) bundle that routes the model-facing **`pwsh` tool to PowerShell 7**
(`pwsh.exe`, major version >= 7) instead of falling back to Windows PowerShell 5.1.

- The executor inherits every behavior of the stock `dsh-pwsh-sandbox` executor: sandbox modes,
  `sandbox_permissions` escalation, denial/runner-failure facts, background jobs, output caps, and
  exit markers. It only replaces executable resolution.
- When PowerShell 7 is missing, a model-facing **`shell_router`** tool reports status, diagnoses
  sandbox problems, and installs PowerShell 7 for the current user or the system, with matching PATH updates.
- In the Web GUI, a **setup dialog** opens whenever PowerShell 7 is missing — on load and again on
  every `pwsh` run — with a download button and live progress (bytes, percent, phase). Closing it
  never cancels an install, and the next failed run re-opens it.

English | [中文说明](https://github.com/drliuhuan/dsh-plugin-pwsh7/blob/main/README.zh.md)

---

## Why

On Windows, DSH mounts `pwsh-sandbox` as `ctx.shell`, but the resolved executable can end up being
Windows PowerShell 5.1 in some environments. This bundle keeps the stock PowerShell executor and
overrides only its `pwshPath` resolution:

1. **Take over the `pwsh-sandbox` slot**: a DSH patch entry's `name` asserts the targeted row, it
   does not replace it, so the stock row is disabled by id and a `RouterPwshExecutor extends
   SandboxPwshExecutor` row (`id: pwsh7-executor`) is inserted. An explicit `config.pwshPath` still
   wins; otherwise the plugin-resolved PowerShell 7 is used.
2. **Insert the bare `dsh-plugin-pwsh7` row**, which registers the `shell_router` tool
   (`status` / `diagnose` / `install`), a small system-prompt section, and the Web setup routes.
   That row's name is also what DSH's client-module scanner uses to discover `client.js`; the
   executor row's `./pwsh-executor` subpath is not a client-bundle source.

## Requirements

- Windows 10/11.
- A DSH profile that supports bundles (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-base` / Web profile). Tested against
  DSH desktop 0.2.1-rc.2.
- Node.js >= 22 is only needed to run the repository test suite.

## Installation

Install from npm through the DSH plugin manager:

```
plugin_manager action=install_bundle target=dsh-plugin-pwsh7@0.2.2
```

Or install from a local checkout (a directory install links the checkout, which is convenient while
developing):

```
plugin_manager action=install_bundle target=D:\path\to\dsh-plugin-pwsh7
```

The new bundle is applied through HMR immediately. After changing the plugin's source, restart DSH
to load a fresh module generation.

## Usage

The model-facing `shell_router` tool:

| Action | What it does |
|---|---|
| `status` (default) | Resolved PowerShell 7 path and version, config file, current sandbox policy, shipped-package resolution. |
| `diagnose` | Runs real PowerShell 7 commands under the **current sandbox policy** (version + workspace write) and reports exit codes, stdout/stderr, denial/runner-failure classification, and concrete hints. |
| `install` | Ensures PowerShell 7 exists. `method: "auto"` (default) prefers the portable zip for the selected scope, then falls back to winget; `portable`/`winget` force one strategy. Existing working installations within the selected scope are reused and their PATH is repaired. |

### Setup dialog (Web)

The browser half renders into DSH's root `shell.overlay` slot, so it works in the ordinary Web GUI
and in the desktop shell without a second window:

- **When it opens:** on first load when `pwsh.exe` cannot be found, and again every time a `pwsh`
  tool run fails for that reason (`missingSeq`). "Not now" hides it until the next failed run; a
  page reload opens it again while PowerShell 7 is still missing.
- **What it does:** `Download and install` starts the same scoped installation job as `shell_router install`.
  The dialog shows `downloading → extracting → verifying`, transferred bytes, total, and percent.
  `Cancel download` aborts it.
- **Why one job:** the dialog and the tool share one coordinator, so a model-triggered install is
  visible in the dialog (with progress) and a dialog-triggered install is awaited by the tool.
  Concurrent installs would race on the same archive under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\dsh\pwsh7\tmp`.
- **Transport:** `GET /pwsh7/state` (snapshot), `GET /pwsh7/events` (SSE, progress coalesced to
  ~7 frames/s), `POST /pwsh7/install`, `POST /pwsh7/cancel`. SSE drives smooth progress; a 3 s
  `/pwsh7/state` poll stays active as the fallback for carriers that buffer event streams.
  These routes are same-origin and accept POST bodies only as `application/json`.
- **Failure:** the dialog keeps the installer's message, offers `Retry`, and links to the official
  PowerShell releases page. A failed install does not affect `pwsh` routing until one succeeds.
- **Scope:** the dialog belongs to the Web GUI. A headless/CLI composition still gets the
  `shell_router` tool and the same installer, just without a window.

### Explicit paths

Resolution order for the pwsh executable:

1. `DSH_PWSH_PATH` environment variable
2. `pwshPath` in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\dsh\pwsh7\config.json`
3. `%ProgramFiles%\PowerShell\7\pwsh.exe`
4. `%LOCALAPPDATA%\dsh\pwsh7\powershell7\…\pwsh.exe` (portable installs, newest first)
5. `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\PowerShell\7\pwsh.exe`
6. every `PATH` entry
7. `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WindowsApps\pwsh.exe` (Store alias)
8. `%ProgramFiles(x86)%\PowerShell\7\pwsh.exe`

The stock `pwsh-sandbox` row still accepts its official `pwshPath` config field; an explicit config
value takes precedence over automatic detection.

### Config file

`%LOCALAPPDATA%\dsh\pwsh7\config.json`:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "pwshPath": "C:\\Program Files\\PowerShell\\7\\pwsh.exe",
  "installed": {
    "pwsh": {
      "path": "C:\\Program Files\\PowerShell\\7\\pwsh.exe",
      "version": "7.6.7",
      "method": "existing",
      "at": "2026-10-17T00:00:00.000Z"
    }
  },
  "updatedAt": "2026-10-17T00:00:00.000Z"
}
```

## Automatic installation

Choose `scope: "user"` (default) or `scope: "system"` in `shell_router install`, or select the scope in the Web dialog.

| Scope | Destination | Persistent PATH |
|---|---|---|
| `user` | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\dsh\pwsh7\powershell7\<version>` | Current user (`HKCU\Environment`) |
| `system` | `%ProgramFiles%\PowerShell\7` | System (`HKLM` environment) |

System installation requires starting the DSH host as administrator; an unelevated host fails before downloading. User installation needs no elevation. Both preserve existing PATH entries and registry value types, avoid duplicate entries, refresh the host process PATH, and notify Windows. Already running terminals may need reopening. PATH write failures are reported as installation failures.

```text
shell_router action=install scope=user
shell_router action=install scope=system
```

Portable download source:

| Component | Source | Destination |
|---|---|---|
| PowerShell 7 | Latest `PowerShell/PowerShell` GitHub release, `PowerShell-*-win-x64.zip` | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\dsh\pwsh7\powershell7\<version>\` |

- HTTPS streaming download into `%LOCALAPPDATA%\dsh\pwsh7\tmp`, with progress callbacks and
  cancellation.
- Extraction uses the Windows built-in `tar.exe` (bsdtar). No downloaded installer is ever executed.
- After extraction the new `pwsh.exe` is executed once to verify a major version >= 7 before it is
  written into `config.json`.
- `auto` falls back to `winget install Microsoft.PowerShell`; when elevation would be required the
  result carries the exact manual elevated command instead of hanging on UAC.
- winget receives `--scope user` or `--scope machine`; fallback never changes the selected scope.
- Live-tested on Windows: 106,364,316-byte zip downloaded in ~31 s, extracted to 244.8 MB, verified
  `7.6.7`.

## Sandbox behavior

- The executor runs through `ctx.sandbox.conf

plugins.description: Ghost-text next-prompt prediction in the DeepSeek Harness Web composer, accepted with Tab.
plugins.readme_text:
# Prompt Forecast

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

Ghost-text prediction of your next action in the DeepSeek Harness Web composer,
in the style of Codex and Claude Code prompt suggestions.

After a completed turn the Host half asks the session's own model for the single
most likely next actionable message, publishes it through a client-visible
session projection, and the Client half renders it as gray text on the first line
of an empty composer. Press **Tab** or **→** to accept it into the draft, or
**Esc** to ignore that suggestion. Typing anything hides it; the text you typed is
never replaced.

The default mode is a Codex-style context fork: the parent's current text
transcript plus one synthetic user turn, `Suggest my next message.`, with
explicit rules that restrict the answer to an action.

## Requirements

- **DSH `0.2.1-rc.2` or newer within `0.2.x`**, declared as `engines.dsh: ^0.2.1-rc.2`.
- This plugin is built on the 0.2.1-rc.2 client and Host surfaces: the
  `conversation.input.overlay` composer slot, `InputActions.captureInsertion()` /
  `insertText()`, and the session-projection carrier fed by `agent/turn-stopping`.
- `dsh plugin add` validates the range during installation and restores the
  previous profile state when it does not match; profile startup checks it
  again. An unmet range refuses to load the plugin; upgrade DSH or install a
  plugin release whose `engines.dsh` matches your runtime. A DSH `0.3` release
  will need a matching plugin release rather than an exemption.

## What it does

- Fork mode (default) predicts from the full text transcript; digest mode uses a
  compact JSON excerpt.
- Predicts the next action, not a status report or an outcome guess.
- Writes in the language the user writes in, one short line.
- Uses the route that served the turn (falling back to the profile default
  model), so no extra provider setup is required.
- Skips subagent sessions and turns with no human input.
- Fails silently: a slow, aborted, or failed prediction never surfaces an error
  in the conversation.

## What gets predicted

The target is the next **actionable** message, not a literal continuation of the
conversation. A useful suggestion is one the user would send to tell the
assistant what to do next:

- an instruction: run the tests, fix this error, check the projection cache,
  explain the failure
- a choice or approval: use option A, go ahead, keep it
- a correction: no, change the client side
- a request to explain or diagnose: why does the fork call time out?
- a short report followed by an instruction: restarted, still empty — check the
  logs

Pure status reports, test results, log observations, narration, and guesses about
what might happen are rejected; `NONE` is a valid answer. A conservative
post-filter drops obvious pure-report clauses, and fork mode falls back to the
digest when the result is unusable.

## Prediction modes

`mode: 'fork'` (default) mirrors the Codex composer-prediction shape. It takes
the session's current text transcript — system and developer instructions plus
user/assistant text — drops tool calls, tool results, reasoning, and attachment
blocks, then appends one synthetic user turn:

```text
Suggest my next message.
```

The model's reply becomes the ghost line. No child session or session event is
created; the fork is an in-memory message list for one auxiliary call. A short
action-rules block is appended to the inherited system prompt so the model writes
the user's next instruction rather than a status report. Because the whole
transcript is sent, this mode costs more tokens and needs a larger `timeoutMs`
than the digest mode.

`mode: 'digest'` keeps the earlier lightweight path: a compact JSON excerpt
(`recent_user_messages`, `latest_assistant_reply`, `tools_used`) with a short,
action-oriented system prompt. Use it for cheap predictions or long sessions
where sending the transcript is too expensive.

## Configuration

The row's `config` block in `cordis.patch.yml` overrides every default:

| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` | `false` leaves the Host half unregistered |
| `mode` | `fork` | `fork` = full transcript + `Suggest my next message.`; `digest` = compact JSON excerpt |
| `maxTokens` | `1024` | Output budget of the prediction request |
| `temperature` | `0.4` | Sampling temperature |
| `timeoutMs` | `12000` | Hard bound on the request; a slower answer is dropped |
| `maxPromptChars` | `80` | Clip length of the predicted prompt |
| `maxForkChars` | `12000` | Character budget of the forked conversation window (system/developer text is always kept) |
| `fallback` | `true` | When the fork yields no text, retry with the compact digest |
| `maxInputChars` | `6000` | Digest-mode excerpt size bound |
| `skipSubagents` | `true` | Subagent sessions get no prediction |
| `provider` | turn route | Explicit provider override |
| `model` | turn route | Explicit model override |

The prediction is produced while the turn boundary is still open
(`agent/turn-stopping`), so its text arrives with the finished turn instead of
requiring a poll. `timeoutMs` is the price: a prediction that does not settle
within that budget is dropped and the turn finishes without one.

## Install

### From GitHub (no build step)

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:littepointR/dsh-prompt-forecast
dsh web
```

`dsh plugin add` forwards to pnpm in the chosen profile, installs the package,
and automatically adds the bundle to `dsh.profile.bundles` because the package
declares `dsh.bundle.patch`. Restart the profile for the plugin to load. The
package is plain JavaScript with no `prepare` build script, so a git install
needs no extra pnpm build approval.

To pin the tagged release:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:littepointR/dsh-prompt-forecast#v0.2.4
```

The Desktop application's `desktop` profile is reserved for the Electron app, so
the CLI rejects `--profile desktop`. Use Settings → Plugins there, or install
into a CLI profile.

### From a local checkout

Use Plugin Manager with this package directory as the bundle target. The bundle
patch inserts the `prompt-forecast` row; it survives restarts because it is a
normal profile bundle.

## Limits

- Only an empty composer shows a suggestion. Completing a partially typed draft
  needs caret geometry the slot does not expose yet and is not part of this
  version.
- The suggestion is a hint, not an action: accepting inserts plain text into the
  draft and nothing is sent.
- Prediction quality depends on the session model; a very small model may return
  a generic follow-up.

## Development

```bash
node --test test/host.test.mjs test/client.test.mjs
node --check index.js && node --check client.js
```

- `index.js` — Host half: generate at `agent/turn-stopping`, publish through the
  `promptForecast` projection.
- `client.js` — Client half: register in `conversation.input.overlay`, render the
  ghost line, handle Tab/→/Esc.
- `test/host.test.mjs` — text normalization, digest building, projection fold.
- `test/client.test.mjs` — structural smoke test of the Client render branches
  (no DOM emulation).

## License

MIT

DSH Crew

A DeepSeek Harness plugin: dispatch work to DSH agents from Claude Code / Codex / Antigravity / Grok, without giving up the host's native subagent UI.
Native Progress UI • Tier Policy & Escalation • Dispatch Guardrails • Jobs Board • In-Host DSH Sessions • Vision & Image Gen (Native-First) • One-Click Install

npm: @zseven-w/dsh-crew · Current plugin release: 0.1.0-rc.11 · Tested with DSH 0.1.1-rc.1

English · 简体中文 · 繁體中文 · 日本語 · 한국어 · Français · Español · Deutsch · Português · Русский · हिन्दी · Türkçe · ไทย · Tiếng Việt · Bahasa Indonesia


The DSH Crew settings page — host integrations, dispatch policy, execution and the multimodal bridge

## Why DSH Crew DSH Crew is a plugin for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH) — an open-source agent harness. It makes DSH agents dispatchable from Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity and Grok: the orchestrator keeps its own model, the work runs on a real DSH agent with that harness's tools, sandbox, presets and session history, and the host still shows it as a native subagent with live progress. What runs the work is a DSH agent, not a bare model call. Tiers (`flash` / `pro`) select how much capability that agent gets from the harness's configured roster — DeepSeek V4 Flash and V4 Pro today — so a change of model in DSH needs no change here.
### 🧵 Native Progress UI Workers appear as regular subagents in Claude Code / Codex / Antigravity / Grok — dispatch count, running step, tool calls and token usage all show up in the host's own task panel, plus a claude-hud statusline segment: `⚙dsh 1▶pro 2m14s 21.7k/606 ✓3`. ### 🎚️ Tier Policy and Escalation `flash` for mechanical work, `pro` for reasoning, `effort` from `off` to `max`. `tier_policy` can clamp every dispatch to one tier at the tool layer, and `escalate_on_failure` retries a failed flash run once on pro — based on evidence, not on guessing difficulty up front.
### 🏛️ In-Host DSH Sessions With the bundle installed in a DSH profile, each worker is a first-class DSH session: visible in the Web UI, grouped by working directory, mounted with the Agent preset you choose per tier. Without DSH running, dispatch falls back to a standalone DSH runtime, so CI and headless environments still work. ### 👁️ Vision and Image Generation DSH's models are text-only. `describe_image` now prefers DeepSeek's own VL model (`deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp`) whenever a key is available, then falls back to the CLIs you already have — Claude, Codex, Grok, Antigravity — or any OpenAI-compatible API you configure. `generate_image` borrows the same CLIs' brush. Pasted images stay visible in the conversation and reach the model as text.
### 🛡️ Dispatch Guardrails Every dispatch is checked before anything spawns. Worker→worker nesting is capped at origin-chain depth 3 and cycles are refused; a second worker on a workspace another job already holds is refused with the holder's info — never silently queued. Refusals are readable errors: wait or re-scope, don't bypass. ### 📋 Jobs Board The DSH Crew panel doubles as a jobs board: every worker job — running or finished — is listed with tier, effort, live progress and tokens, held workspaces show their holders, and a job that vanishes mid-flight (e.g. a hub restart) is surfaced as an orphan ghost instead of disappearing silently.
### 🔌 Custom Providers Bring your own endpoint (Base URL + API key + models) or a local command template. Each provider has a connectivity test that checks reachability and auth, then makes one real vision call so you find out now, not mid-task. ### 📦 One-Click Install The settings page installs and updates the Claude Code plugin, the Codex role files and the Antigravity / Grok agents, skills and commands for you — marketplace registration, permission allowlist, HUD wiring, absolute paths rendered for this machine — and restores them just as easily. Every settings file is backed up first.
## How it works ``` Claude Code / Codex / Antigravity / Grok (orchestrator, keeps its own model) └─ ds-flash / ds-pro ← native subagent shell (progress shows in the host's task UI) └─ MCP: dsh_run_worker(tier, effort, cwd, worker=) ├─ worker="agy"/"grok" → that external CLI runs the task (explicit opt-in) ├─ hub reachable → session inside DSH (visible in the Web UI, grouped by cwd) └─ otherwise → dsh-jsonrpc-agent runtime (worker.cordis.yml) └─ DeepSeek V4 Flash / Pro (DSH SDK, event stream → progress and token stats) ``` ## One run, two views Dispatch fans out. Below, eighteen workers translate this README in parallel: the host counts them as its own subagents, while the harness runs them as real sessions.

Claude Code sees dsh-crew workers as native subagents, with a statusline segment tracking running tiers, elapsed time and tokens.

The DSH Crew panel sees the same run from the harness side: which host dispatched each job, its tier and effort, live progress and token usage.

The panel is also the jobs board: running and finished jobs stay listed with tier, progress and tokens, held workspaces name their holders, and a job that vanishes mid-flight (a hub restart) surfaces as an orphan ghost instead of disappearing silently.

## Install Install into a DSH profile from npm: ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add @zseven-w/dsh-crew@latest dsh web ``` Or, for local development straight from the source tree: ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add link:/path/to/dsh-crew dsh web ``` The `link:` protocol symlinks the profile dependency to this repository, so rebuilds are visible immediately. ### Configure DeepSeek credentials (standalone only) In hub mode — the installation above — workers run inside the DSH instance and use the DeepSeek credentials it is already configured with. Nothing else to set up. Only the standalone fallback needs a key of its own: dispatching from a host with no DSH instance running launches a worker runtime as a separate process. Obtain an API key from [platform.deepseek.com](https://platform.deepseek.com) and write it to `~/.config/dsh-crew/.env`: ``` DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=sk-... ``` ### Verify ```bash node scripts/smoke.mjs ``` The smoke test dispatches one cheap job through whichever path is available — the hub when a DSH instance is running, s

plugins.description: Noema long-term memory plugin for DSH: durable, inspectable agent memory with recall tools and a settings page.
plugins.readme_text:
DSH Noema

Long-term memory for DeepSeek Harness — durable, inspectable agent memory backed by Noema.
Recall Before Work • Import From 9 Agent Tools • Settings-Page Memory Management • Crash Keep-Alive • Hot Reload

npm: @zseven-w/dsh-noema · Tested with DSH 0.2.0-rc.2

English · 简体中文 · 繁體中文 · 日本語 · 한국어 · Français · Español · Deutsch · Português · Русский · हिन्दी · Türkçe · ไทย · Tiếng Việt · Bahasa Indonesia


The Noema Memory settings page — import sources, memory management, and live server status

## Why DSH Noema DSH Noema connects [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) with [Noema](https://github.com/ZSeven-W/noema) — a local-first, non-vector memory system for coding agents — so an Agent keeps durable knowledge across sessions instead of starting every conversation from zero.
### 🧠 Durable Recall Memories persist as inspectable Markdown files under `NOEMA_ROOT` (default `~/.agent-memory/`). `noema_recall` loads relevant context at the start of a session; `noema_search`, `noema_browse`, `noema_catalog`, and `noema_recall_graph` cover lookup, exploration, and auditing. ### 📥 Import From Other Tools `noema_import` reads the memory files of ten other AI coding tools — Codex, Claude Code, opencode, Cursor, Grok, WorkBuddy, Antigravity, Trae, Qoder, Hermes — splits them into sections, and saves each as a durable memory. A content-keyed ledger deduplicates across runs and across tools that share files.
### 🛠️ Settings-Page Management The Noema Memory settings page configures the server command, memory root, budgets, idle/call timeouts, and the guidance section — and a Manage memories card searches, browses, adds, reviews, and deletes stored memories directly. ### 🩺 Keep-Alive The memory server stays up: idle timeout defaults to never, and a keep-alive loop restarts the `noema-mcp` child in the background when it crashes or exits, with a configurable check interval and restart backoff.
### 🔍 Smart Entity Extraction Noema's extraction engine combines jieba word segmentation with high-precision signals — English proper nouns, CJK names and technical terms, quoted topics, and repetition — with stopword and path filters, so the PageIndex topic catalog stays clean. ### ⚡ Hot Reload After the first boot, the plugin never needs a restart again: `pnpm run build` hot-reloads the host plugin through Cordis HMR, and `ppnpm run build:client` hot-swaps the browser bundle over the client-hmr SSE channel.
## Install into DSH ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add @zseven-w/dsh-noema@latest dsh web ``` Or, for local development straight from the source tree: ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add link:/path/to/dsh-noema dsh web ``` The `link:` protocol symlinks the profile dependency to this repository, so rebuilds are visible immediately and Cordis HMR can watch the compiled output. The plugin bundles the `noema-mcp` binary through per-platform optional npm packages. To build it yourself instead, run `cargo build --release -p noema-mcp` inside the bundled `noema` submodule, or point the Server command setting at any `noema-mcp` build. ## Memory Tools The model-facing tools mirror the Noema MCP surface: | Tool | What it does | | --- | --- | | `noema_recall` | Recall relevant memories for a query, with a token budget. | | `noema_search` | Full-text search over stored memories. | | `noema_browse` | Browse the PageIndex catalog for a topic or entity. | | `noema_catalog` | Render the full memory catalog as markdown. | | `noema_recall_graph` | Multi-hop recall through links and shared entities. | | `noema_neighbors` | One graph hop from a memory. | | `noema_explain` | Explain why a memory was or was not recalled. | | `noema_remember` | Save a durable fact, decision, constraint, or preference. | | `noema_review_list` | List pending review candidates. | | `noema_review_decide` | Accept, reject, edit, or merge a candidate. | | `noema_forget` | Tombstone or hard-delete a memory. | | `noema_policy_get` / `noema_policy_set` | Read or update the write policy. | | `noema_status` | Server and tenant status: counts, index health, storage root. | | `noema_import` | Import memories from other AI coding tools. | Each tool returns a uniform envelope `{ ok, tool, text }` where `text` carries the full server output. ## Import memories from other tools | Source id | Global files | Workspace files | | --- | --- | --- | | `codex` | `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` + the Codex memory pipeline: `~/.codex/memories/MEMORY.md`, `memory_summary.md`, `rollout_summaries/*.md`, `extensions/ad_hoc/notes/*.md` (`raw_memories.md` skipped — it is the uncurated feed) | `AGENTS.md`, `AGENTS.local.md` | | `claude-code` | `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `~/.claude/CLAUDE.local.md`, `~/.claude/MEMORY.md` | `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`, `MEMORY.md` | | `opencode` | `~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md` | `AGENTS.md` | | `cursor` | `~/.cursor/rules/*.mdc`, `~/.cursorrules` | `.cursor/rules/*.mdc`, `.cursorrules` | | `grok` | `~/.grok/AGENTS.md` + the Grok cross-session memory: `~/.grok/memory/MEMORY.md`, per-project `MEMORY.md`, and `sessions/*.md` summaries | `AGENTS.md` | | `workbuddy` | `~/.codebuddy/CODEBUDDY.md` (WorkBuddy memory file), `~/.workbuddy/AGENTS.md`, `~/.workbuddy/memory.md`, `~/.config/workbuddy/AGENTS.md`, `~/Library/Application Support/WorkBuddy/AGENTS.md` | `AGENTS.md`, `CODEBUDDY.md` | | `antigravity` | `~/.antigravity/AGENTS.md`, `~/.config/antigravity/AGENTS.md`, `~/Library/Application Support/Antigravity/AGENTS.md` (best-effort; no documented global memory store yet) | `AGENTS.md`, `AGENTS.local.md` | | `trae` | `~/.trae/AGENTS.md`, `~/.trae/memory/`, `~/.trae/rules/` (plus the `~/.trae-cn` variants) | `AGENTS.md`, `.trae/rules/` | | `qoder` | `~/.qoder-cn/AGENTS.md`, `~/.qoder-cn/rules/`, the auto-memory roots `~/.qoder-cn/memory/` and `~/.qoder-cn/projects/*/memory/` (plus `~/.qoder` variants) | `AGENTS.md`, `AGENTS.local.md`, `.qoder/rules/` | | `hermes` | `~/.hermes/memories/` (`MEMORY.md` + `USER.md`) and the global `~/.hermes/SOUL.md` | `.hermes.md`, `HERMES.md`,
